warhammer-40k.rule.warp-translation.go_wrong: A ship without a Navigator may lose track of position, distance, and destination.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-translation.who_may: Ships travelling between real space and warp space
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-translation.combines: Navigator guidance, warp drives, Gellar Fields

warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.name: Geller Field protection

effect.summary: A Geller Field creates a small bubble of reality that warp denizens cannot pierce.

warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.cost_or_limit: Protection depends on the field functioning.
warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.go_wrong: A failure can expose the ship to warp intrusion; permanent failure is likely unsurvivable.
warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.where_from: The account of warp travel and ship defenses.
warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.combines: The field protects a ship while it travels through the warp.
warhammer-40k.rule.geller-field-protecti.blocked_reason: It requires a sustained defensive field covering a ship and excluding warp beings.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.name: Warp breach and possession

effect.summary: Warp entities that get aboard may possess weak-minded people, manifest, or mutate victims, depending on their strength.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.cost_or_limit: The outcome depends on the intruding entity’s strength and the victim’s will.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.go_wrong: Intrusion can cause havoc, madness, mutation, or loss of the ship.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.mind: A weak-minded soul may be possessed.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.who_may: Warp entities that breach a ship’s defenses.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.combines: A Geller Field failure can permit the breach.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.mechanism: Possession and bodily mutation by warp entities.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-breach-and-posse.blocked_reason: Possession requires an entity to take control of a person’s mind or body.

warhammer-40k.rule.component-space-and-p.name: Component Space and Power

effect.summary: A ship has finite room and generated power; a component needs both to function.

warhammer-40k.rule.component-space-and-p.cost_or_limit: Components cannot exceed the hull’s Space or the drive’s Power.
warhammer-40k.rule.component-space-and-p.go_wrong: An unpowered component provides no benefits; an over-capacity component cannot be contained within the hull.
warhammer-40k.rule.component-space-and-p.combines: Hull determines Space; the plasma drive supplies Power.
warhammer-40k.rule.component-space-and-p.blocked_reason: This is a capacity constraint that can be tracked as a game rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.unpowered-components.name: Unpowered Components

effect.summary: An unpowered component has no light, power, gravity, or air and grants no ship benefits.

warhammer-40k.rule.unpowered-components.cost_or_limit: The component must receive power to function.
warhammer-40k.rule.unpowered-components.go_wrong: Occupants need void-suits to enter an unpowered section.
warhammer-40k.rule.unpowered-components.combines: A component becomes unpowered when its Power requirement is unmet.
warhammer-40k.rule.unpowered-components.blocked_reason: The component’s powered or unpowered state changes its function and environment.

warhammer-40k.rule.exposed-components.name: Exposed Components

effect.summary: A component without enough hull Space is mounted outside the ship and lacks hull protection.

warhammer-40k.rule.exposed-components.cost_or_limit: It must still receive power to function.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposed-components.go_wrong: In combat, it absorbs the first hit past the shields and is destroyed; occupants are killed.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposed-components.combines: An external component is specially designed for outside mounting and is protected from destruction except by a Critical Hit.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposed-components.blocked_reason: The rule depends on whether an item is contained within a vessel and how that changes its vulnerability.

warhammer-40k.rule.external-component.name: External Component

effect.summary: A specially designed outside-mounted component uses no Space and can only be destroyed by a Critical Hit.

warhammer-40k.rule.external-component.cost_or_limit: It must be designed with the external trait.
warhammer-40k.rule.external-component.combines: May be powered and used while mounted outside the hull.
warhammer-40k.rule.external-component.mechanism: Special component placement and damage protection.
warhammer-40k.rule.external-component.blocked_reason: This depends on item placement relative to a vessel and a special protection condition.

warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.name: Crew Population and Morale maximum

effect.summary: Components may raise Crew Population or Morale above 100, setting a new maximum that restoration cannot exceed.

warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.cost_or_limit: Restoration stops at the ship’s new maximum.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.combines: Components can increase the maximum values; damage and losses can reduce them.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.blocked_reason: This is a numerical cap on recovery.

warhammer-40k.rule.essential-component-r.name: Essential Component requirement

effect.summary: A starship needs exactly one component from every essential category or it loses a vital function.

warhammer-40k.rule.essential-component-r.cost_or_limit: One, and no more than one, from each category.
warhammer-40k.rule.essential-component-r.go_wrong: Missing components leave ship functions absent.
warhammer-40k.rule.essential-component-r.combines: Categories include drives, warp engines, fields, shields, bridge, life support, quarters, and sensors.
warhammer-40k.rule.essential-component-r.blocked_reason: This is a direct equipment restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-capacity-slots.name: Weapon Capacity slots

effect.summary: Weapon components must fit an available ship weapon slot; small ships need a prow slot for lances.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-capacity-slots.cost_or_limit: A ship cannot exceed its listed number and type of weapon slots.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-capacity-slots.go_wrong: A lance cannot be installed on a small ship without a prow slot.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-capacity-slots.combines: Restricts weapon placement by hull class and slot.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-capacity-slots.blocked_reason: The restriction is explicit and directly enforceable.

warhammer-40k.rule.supplemental-componen.name: Supplemental Component duplication

effect.summary: Multiple components of a type may be installed unless a specific entry forbids duplicates.

warhammer-40k.rule.supplemental-componen.cost_or_limit: Some components are explicitly limited to one per ship.
warhammer-40k.rule.supplemental-componen.combines: Weapon installation also obeys slot restrictions.
warhammer-40k.rule.supplemental-componen.blocked_reason: The rule defines a direct installation constraint.

warhammer-40k.rule.additional-facilities.name: Additional Facilities installation limit

effect.summary: Each listed Additional Facility may be installed only once on a starship.

warhammer-40k.rule.additional-facilities.cost_or_limit: One of each facility per ship.
warhammer-40k.rule.additional-facilities.combines: Applies to the listed Additional Facilities.
warhammer-40k.rule.additional-facilities.blocked_reason: The rule defines a direct installation constraint.

warhammer-40k.rule.ghost-field-and-void-.name: Ghost Field and Void Shield choice

effect.summary: At combat start, a ship with a Ghost Field must choose to use it or its Void Shields.

warhammer-40k.rule.ghost-field-and-void-.cost_or_limit: The two defences cannot operate together.
warhammer-40k.rule.ghost-field-and-void-.go_wrong: Choosing one leaves the other unavailable for that combat.
warhammer-40k.rule.ghost-field-and-void-.combines: Ghost Field conflicts with Void Shields.
warhammer-40k.rule.ghost-field-and-void-.blocked_reason: It requires selecting between two incompatible active defences.

warhammer-40k.rule.ship-point-constructi.name: Ship Point construction limit

effect.summary: A newly built ship’s hull and component costs cannot exceed the group’s Ship Point total.

warhammer-40k.rule.ship-point-constructi.cost_or_limit: Essential components are generally free; certain specialised ones cost Ship Points.
warhammer-40k.rule.ship-point-constructi.go_wrong: Unused points become starting Profit Factor.
warhammer-40k.rule.ship-point-constructi.combines: Component rarity and price are related to Ship Point cost.
warhammer-40k.rule.ship-point-constructi.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward resource limit.

warhammer-40k.rule.post-construction-com.name: Post-construction component limit

effect.summary: After ship creation, available Space, Power, and Profit Factor limit new components rather than Ship Points.

warhammer-40k.rule.post-construction-com.cost_or_limit: Components must fit the ship’s remaining Space and Power.
warhammer-40k.rule.post-construction-com.go_wrong: Components that exceed capacity become unpowered or exposed.
warhammer-40k.rule.post-construction-com.combines: Plasma drives supply Power; hulls supply Space.
warhammer-40k.rule.post-construction-com.blocked_reason: The stated capacity constraints are directly enforceable.

warhammer-40k.rule.plasma-drive-power-ge.name: Plasma drive power generation

effect.summary: Plasma drives propel ships and provide their Power rating rather than having a Power requirement themselves.

warhammer-40k.rule.plasma-drive-power-ge.cost_or_limit: Other components draw from the generated Power.
warhammer-40k.rule.plasma-drive-power-ge.go_wrong: Insufficient Power leaves a component unpowered or exposed.
warhammer-40k.rule.plasma-drive-power-ge.combines: Power supply depends on the installed drive.
warhammer-40k.rule.plasma-drive-power-ge.blocked_reason: The mechanism is a direct capacity rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.hull-space-capacity.name: Hull Space capacity

effect.summary: A ship’s hull sets its available Space for components.

warhammer-40k.rule.hull-space-capacity.cost_or_limit: Components must fit the hull’s total Space.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-space-capacity.go_wrong: Excess Space requirements cannot be installed normally.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-space-capacity.combines: Space capacity is supplied by the hull, not by components.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-space-capacity.blocked_reason: The mechanism is a direct capacity rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-immobil.name: Space station immobility

effect.summary: A space station cannot move in realspace or the warp and never takes Manoeuvre actions.

warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-immobil.cost_or_limit: Stations use a distinct essential-component set: hull, generator, shields, bridge, and life support.

warhammer-40k.rule.orky-tek.name: Orky Tek

effect.summary: Only an Ork crew can pilot the ship, and its components fail when installed on non-Ork ships.

warhammer-40k.rule.orky-tek.cost_or_limit: Non-Orks cannot pilot; components are restricted to Ork vessels.
warhammer-40k.rule.orky-tek.go_wrong: Components cease functioning on other ships.
warhammer-40k.rule.orky-tek.combines: Applies to Ork technology and the Onslaught Raider.
warhammer-40k.rule.orky-tek.blocked_reason: The rule is a direct use restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-essenti.name: Space station Essential Components

effect.summary: A station requires a hull, generator, Void Shield Array, bridge, and Life Sustainer instead of the normal starship set.

warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-essenti.go_wrong: Missing required components leave station functions absent.
warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-essenti.combines: Works with the station immobility rule.
warhammer-40k.rule.space-station-essenti.blocked_reason: This is a direct equipment restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.void-shields.name: Void shields

effect.summary: Shields cancel incoming hits until overloaded, then recover for later attackers.

warhammer-40k.rule.void-shields.cost_or_limit: Each shield absorbs one hit before overloading for the current salvo.
warhammer-40k.rule.void-shields.combines: Applies against ship weapons, including lances and macrobatteries.
warhammer-40k.rule.void-shields.blocked_reason: The shield's hit-count limit and recovery can be represented as a basic block effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.name: Hull Integrity

effect.summary: Damage exceeding Armour reduces Hull Integrity and also costs crew and morale.

warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.cost_or_limit: Each Hull Integrity lost also removes one Crew Population and one Morale.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.go_wrong: At zero Hull Integrity, the ship is Crippled.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.combines: Damage is reduced by Armour first.
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.mechanism: ship hit points with linked crew losses
warhammer-40k.rule.hull-integrity.blocked_reason: The damage and linked losses are straightforward resource reduction.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.name: Critical Hits

effect.summary: A qualifying blow causes a listed ship-system or hull consequence.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.cost_or_limit: Triggered by meeting a weapon's Crit Rating or damaging a crippled ship past Armour.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.go_wrong: Results can disable, destroy, depressurise, or ignite ship components.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.who_may: Attackers who know of the target component may select it where allowed.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.combines: Active Augury or a component's use can reveal it to an attacker.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-hits.blocked_reason: A trigger and table of consequences can be represented as game rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.crippled.name: Crippled

effect.summary: At zero Hull Integrity, a ship suffers reduced handling, detection, speed, and weapon strength.

warhammer-40k.rule.crippled.cost_or_limit: The condition lasts until at least one Hull Integrity is restored.
warhammer-40k.rule.crippled.go_wrong: Further damage past Armour causes a Critical Hit.
warhammer-40k.rule.crippled.combines: Crew Population can also cause a ship to count as crippled.
warhammer-40k.rule.crippled.blocked_reason: The condition applies a defined set of ongoing penalties.

warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.name: Zero gravity

effect.summary: Movement is halved, and charging or running risks uncontrolled drifting.

warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.cost_or_limit: Movement actions require a nearby secure surface to push from.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.go_wrong: A failed hard Agility test while charging or running causes loss of control.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.who_may: Characters in zero gravity, except for the stated Void Born exception
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.combines: Void Born characters ignore its movement penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-gravity.blocked_reason: The passage states discrete movement penalties and a test trigger.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.name: Warp drive explosion

effect.summary: The explosion opens a rift and can damage or draw in nearby ships.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.cost_or_limit: Ships within stated distances make piloting tests to avoid the effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.go_wrong: Nearby ships may be struck or sucked into the rift, with possession and daemon manifestations possible.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.combines: Void shields do not protect against the described lance-equivalent strike.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.mechanism: catastrophic area hazard and spatial rift
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-explosion.blocked_reason: The rift's spatial and supernatural consequences exceed the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.fire.name: Fire

effect.summary: An uncontrolled fire damages a component and spreads to another component.

warhammer-40k.rule.fire.cost_or_limit: It must be controlled within one Strategic Turn to avoid consuming its component and spreading.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.go_wrong: Crew Population and Morale fall; the ship is destroyed if every component burns.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.mind: Crew morale is harmed by the fire.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.who_may: Characters can organise firefighting or the captain can vent the compartment.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.where_from: A ship component that catches fire
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.combines: Venting extinguishes it but depressurises the component.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire.blocked_reason: The fire spreads through connected ship components as an area hazard.

warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.name: Depressurisation

effect.summary: Air vents from a component, leaving its occupants exposed to vacuum.

warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.cost_or_limit: The venting period depends on the size of the breach; airtight hatches confine it to one component.
warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.go_wrong: Occupants suffer vacuum effects, while crew and morale are reduced.
warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.where_from: A breached or deliberately vented ship component
warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.combines: A component can be depressurised without being damaged.
warhammer-40k.rule.depressurisation.blocked_reason: It affects occupants across a compartment and depends on the compartment's pressure state.

warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.name: Crew Population and Morale

effect.summary: Crew and morale values decline from events and impose threshold-based ship penalties.

warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.cost_or_limit: Both begin at 100; effects reverse when values rise above their relevant thresholds, and restoration cannot exceed maximum values.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.go_wrong: At zero population the ship cannot operate; at zero morale the crew rises against its authorities.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.mind: Morale measures crew loyalty and commitment.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.combines: Losses from damage and hazards affect these values.
warhammer-40k.rule.crew-population-and-m.blocked_reason: Values, thresholds, and reversibility are directly representable as resource rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.name: Mutiny

effect.summary: Low morale can trigger rebellion against the captain or other authorities.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.cost_or_limit: The captain tests when morale falls below 70, 40, or 10; during combat, only one test follows the combat even if several thresholds are crossed.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.go_wrong: If mutineers win repeatedly, especially by three degrees, they take the ship.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.mind: Crew disloyalty and rebellion are central to the event.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.who_may: Crew members may rebel; characters may try to suppress them.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.combines: Suppression may use Command, Charm, or Intimidation.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutiny.blocked_reason: The outcome depends on crew loyalty and coordinated rebellion, which is more than a basic physical effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-jams.name: Weapon Jams

effect.summary: A sufficiently high unmodified ranged attack roll can jam a weapon; clearing it takes an action and successful test, and loses its loaded ammunition.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-jams.cost_or_limit: A jammed weapon cannot fire until cleared; failed clearing attempts can be retried on later rounds.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-jams.go_wrong: The weapon remains jammed after a failed clearing test.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-jams.combines: Automatic misses and certain firing modes can also trigger jams.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-jams.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar cannot represent a weapon’s jammed state or its clearing and ammunition-loss procedure.

warhammer-40k.rule.wounds.name: Wounds

effect.summary: Each point of damage suffered adds one Wound; reaching maximum Wounds limits actions and risks unconsciousness.

warhammer-40k.rule.wounds.go_wrong: At the maximum, further attacks cause Critical Wounds; the character may fall unconscious.
warhammer-40k.rule.wounds.combines: Maximum Wounds depend on Strength, Toughness, and Willpower bonuses.
warhammer-40k.rule.wounds.blocked_reason: A vitality counter and threshold can represent the described effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage.name: Damage

effect.summary: Damage accumulates and remains until natural healing or medical care removes it.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage.cost_or_limit: Incoming damage is normally reduced by Toughness and applicable armour; some sources bypass either.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage.go_wrong: Damage beyond the Wounds threshold causes Critical Damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage.combines: Armour, Toughness, damage types, Wounds, and critical effects determine outcomes.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar cannot represent damage accumulation, reduction, healing, and threshold-based consequences.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-types.name: Damage Types

effect.summary: Damage is classified by type, which determines the relevant critical effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-types.combines: Type combines with hit location and critical damage to select effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-types.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar does not represent damage-type-dependent critical effect tables.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.name: Critical Damage

effect.summary: Damage beyond a character’s Wounds triggers cumulative critical injury effects selected by location and damage type.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.cost_or_limit: Critical effects can have different durations, including permanent ones, and persist until healing or medical attention.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.go_wrong: Further damage increases the critical total and applies a new set of effects; the character may die.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.who_may: Characters whose damage exceeds their Wounds
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.combines: Uses damage type, hit location, total critical damage, and the critical effect tables.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-damage.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar cannot model cumulative critical injury, body locations, or table-driven consequences.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.name: Damage recovery

effect.summary: Characters recover ordinary and Critical Damage over time; medical care and some psychic powers can also remove it, with recovery rates determined by several factors.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.cost_or_limit: Recovery rate depends on the method and other factors.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.who_may: Characters; medical attention and some psychic powers can assist.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.where_from: Natural healing, medical care, or psychic powers.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.combines: Healing details are referenced on page 262.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-recovery.blocked_reason: The rule describes damage removal over time.

warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.name: Fatigue capacity and collapse

effect.summary: Fatigue imposes a –10 penalty to all Tests; exceeding Toughness Bonus causes unconsciousness, after which fatigue resets to that bonus.

warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.cost_or_limit: A character can function up to their Toughness Bonus in Fatigue levels; excess causes unconsciousness for 10 minus Toughness Bonus minutes.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.go_wrong: Excess fatigue causes collapse and unconsciousness.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.mind: Unconsciousness until the stated interval passes.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.where_from: Attacks, Grappling, Critical Effects, and strenuous Actions.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.combines: On waking, Fatigue resets to the character’s Toughness Bonus.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-capacity-and-.blocked_reason: The threshold, penalty, and timed unconsciousness can be represented as game states.

warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-recovery.name: Fatigue recovery

effect.summary: An hour of qualifying rest removes one Fatigue level; eight consecutive hours remove all levels.

warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-recovery.cost_or_limit: Rest must exclude combat, psychic powers, and other strenuous activity.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-recovery.combines: Unconscious time does not count as rest.
warhammer-40k.rule.fatigue-recovery.blocked_reason: The rule specifies conditions and a recovery rate.

warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.name: Characteristic Damage limits

effect.summary: Characteristic Damage cannot reduce a Characteristic below zero and may also affect its corresponding Bonus.

warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.cost_or_limit: Characteristic scores cannot fall below zero from this damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.go_wrong: Reaching zero causes a characteristic-specific consequence.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.mind: Some zero-score outcomes include coma, nightmare sleep, or catatonia.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.who_may: Characters affected by certain powers, poisons, diseases, or hazards.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.combines: Zero-score outcomes are listed by Characteristic.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.blocked_reason: A score floor and threshold outcomes fit the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.name: Zero Characteristic Scores

effect.summary: At zero, Weapon Skill or Ballistic Skill tests are unavailable; Strength causes unconsciousness; Toughness causes death; Agility causes paralysis; Intelligence causes coma; Perception removes senses; Willpower causes nightmare sleep and an Insanity Point; Fellowship causes catatonia.

warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.cost_or_limit: The consequence depends on which Characteristic reaches zero.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.go_wrong: Zero Toughness is fatal; other scores impose the listed incapacities or penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.mind: Intelligence, Willpower, and Fellowship have distinct severe mental or social consequences.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.who_may: Characters whose relevant Characteristic reaches zero.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.combines: Perception zero carries a –30 penalty to Tests except Toughness; Willpower zero grants an Insanity Point on waking.
warhammer-40k.rule.zero-characteristic-s.blocked_reason: The listed threshold outcomes can be represented as status changes and penalties.

warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.name: Characteristic Damage recovery

effect.summary: Unless specified otherwise, one point of Characteristic Damage heals each hour regardless of activity; medical attention may speed recovery.

warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.cost_or_limit: One point per hour by default.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.where_from: Automatic recovery; medical care may accelerate it.
warhammer-40k.rule.characteristic-damage.blocked_reason: The rule gives a straightforward recovery rate.

warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.name: Amputation treatment and infection

effect.summary: A lost body part causes Blood Loss and needs prompt treatment; without a medic, the stump has a 20% chance to heal, otherwise infection kills the character after 1d10 days.

warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.cost_or_limit: Without a medic, stump healing has a 20% chance; successful survival delays damage recovery by 1d10+2 days.
warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.go_wrong: An unhealed stump causes death from infection after 1d10 days.
warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.who_may: Characters who lose a body part other than the head; Medicae-skilled helpers can treat them.
warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.combines: Blood Loss must also be treated.
warhammer-40k.rule.amputation-treatment-.blocked_reason: The rule is a timed injury consequence with a treatment chance.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.name: Lost hand and arm penalties

effect.summary: A lost hand penalizes tests needing two hands and prevents two-handed weapons; a lost arm has the same effects and prevents strapping on a shield.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.cost_or_limit: A primary-hand loss also penalizes attacks with the secondary hand by –20; spending 100 XP reduces that penalty by 10.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.go_wrong: Losing both hands or arms causes further severe impairment.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.who_may: Characters who lose a hand or arm.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.combines: A shield can be strapped to an injured arm if the hand is lost but the arm remains.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-hand-and-arm-pen.blocked_reason: The effects are persistent penalties and equipment restrictions.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-eye.name: Lost eye

effect.summary: Losing one eye reduces Ballistic Skill by 10 and penalizes sight-dependent tests by –20; losing both causes blindness.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-eye.go_wrong: Loss of both eyes causes blindness.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-eye.who_may: Characters who lose an eye or eyes.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-eye.blocked_reason: The rule is a lasting penalty and status.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.name: Lost foot or leg

effect.summary: A lost foot halves movement and penalizes movement-related actions and tests; losing a leg has the same effects and also prevents using Dodge.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.cost_or_limit: The impairment persists unless addressed by replacement limbs.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.go_wrong: Losing both feet or legs severely limits movement.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.who_may: Characters who lose a foot or leg.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.combines: Replacement limbs may address the loss.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-foot-or-leg.blocked_reason: The rule is a lasting movement penalty and skill restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.blindness.name: Blindness

effect.summary: A blind character automatically fails vision-based tests and Ballistic Skill Tests, and suffers –30 to Weapon Skill and most other tests that benefit from sight.

warhammer-40k.rule.blindness.blocked_reason: The rule specifies test restrictions and penalties.

warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.name: Blood Loss

effect.summary: A character with Blood Loss has a 10% chance to die each Round; a conscious character can attempt Medicae to staunch it.

warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.cost_or_limit: A Difficult (–10) Medicae Test each Round; strenuous activity raises the difficulty to Very Hard (–30).
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.go_wrong: There is a 10% chance of death each Round while untreated.
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.who_may: Characters suffering Blood Loss; the character or another person may attempt treatment.
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.where_from: A Critical Effect or severe injury.
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.combines: Treatment may be attempted each Round.
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.mechanism: recurring death chance and treatment check
warhammer-40k.rule.blood-loss.blocked_reason: The rule uses a recurring chance and a treatment test.

warhammer-40k.rule.deafness.name: Deafness

effect.summary: A deaf character automatically fails tests that rely on hearing until recovery or repair.

warhammer-40k.rule.deafness.combines: Communication with others may be impaired.
warhammer-40k.rule.deafness.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a clear test restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.name: Fire damage and ignition

effect.summary: Fire deals damage each exposed Round; after the first Round of exposure, a Challenging Agility Test is required to avoid catching fire.

warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.cost_or_limit: Ignition checks recur each Round after the first exposure to the same flames.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.go_wrong: A burning character takes 1d10 damage without armour reduction and one Fatigue each Round until extinguished.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.who_may: Characters exposed to flames or specified flame effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.where_from: Environmental fire, Flame weapons, or certain Toxic Critical Effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.combines: Fire damage counts as Energy Damage for determining Critical Effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.fire-damage-and-ignit.blocked_reason: The rule describes recurring damage, a save, and an extinguishing condition.

warhammer-40k.rule.suffocation.name: Suffocation

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.suffocation.cost_or_limit: Breath-holding duration depends on activity and Toughness Bonus; failures cause Fatigue, and prolonged oxygen deprivation causes unconsciousness and then damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.suffocation.combines: Oxygen deprivation can result from drowning, smoke, or toxins.
warhammer-40k.rule.suffocation.blocked_reason: This is a physiological hazard and its consequences can be represented with basic damage and condition effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.vacuum.name: Vacuum

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.vacuum.cost_or_limit: Sudden exposure allows brief survival before depressurisation damage; space adds cold damage. Gradual pressure loss causes escalating Toughness Tests and damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.vacuum.go_wrong: A corpse exposed in space freezes after five rounds and shatters if damaged; return from death is exceptionally rare.
warhammer-40k.rule.vacuum.combines: Suffocation and extreme cold can accompany exposure.
warhammer-40k.rule.vacuum.blocked_reason: The passage suggests return from death may be possible through a Daemonic pact but does not describe how that works.

warhammer-40k.rule.healing.name: Healing

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.healing.cost_or_limit: Light, heavy, and critical damage recover at different rates; critical damage requires medical attention.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing.go_wrong: Critical damage does not recover naturally.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing.where_from: Natural recovery, rest, medical attention, or some psychic powers
warhammer-40k.rule.healing.combines: Bed rest and medical attention can improve recovery.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing.blocked_reason: The recovery process uses damage states and elapsed time without requiring an unsupported effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.low-gravity-worlds.name: Low Gravity Worlds

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.low-gravity-worlds.cost_or_limit: Movement and Initiative use Agility Bonus +2; carrying limits use Strength and Toughness Bonuses +4; throwing uses Strength Bonus +2; jumps and leaps double.
warhammer-40k.rule.low-gravity-worlds.combines: Changes movement, load limits, throwing, jumping, and leaping.
warhammer-40k.rule.low-gravity-worlds.blocked_reason: The passage describes direct changes to physical measures and movement.

warhammer-40k.rule.high-gravity-worlds.name: High Gravity Worlds

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.high-gravity-worlds.cost_or_limit: Movement and Initiative use Agility Bonus −2, minimum 1; carrying limits use Strength and Toughness Bonuses −4, minimum 0; throwing uses Strength Bonus −2, minimum 0; jumps and leaps halve.
warhammer-40k.rule.high-gravity-worlds.combines: Changes movement, load limits, throwing, jumping, and leaping.
warhammer-40k.rule.high-gravity-worlds.blocked_reason: The passage describes direct changes to physical measures and movement.

warhammer-40k.rule.starship-construction.name: Starship construction and acquisition

effect.summary: No effect stated.

warhammer-40k.rule.starship-construction.cost_or_limit: A new ship takes years or decades to build, normally under Imperial Navy control; only one warp-capable ship can be acquired at a time.
warhammer-40k.rule.starship-construction.who_may: Imperial Navy normally builds new vessels; Rogue Traders more often refit or salvage ships.
warhammer-40k.rule.starship-construction.blocked_reason: This is a general restriction that can be represented as a game rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.name: Insanity and Corruption reach 100

effect.summary: At 100 Insanity or Corruption Points, the character’s career and life end as if killed.

warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.cost_or_limit: Either score reaching 100 triggers the endpoint.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.mind: Insanity drives madness; Corruption taints the soul.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.who_may: Characters accumulating Insanity or Corruption Points.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.combines: Both tracks share this terminal threshold.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-and-corrupti.blocked_reason: A numeric threshold ending play is directly representable as a rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.name: Insanity Points thresholds

effect.summary: Every 10 Insanity Points calls for a Trauma Test; totals of 40, 60, and 80 grant disorders of increasing severity.

warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.cost_or_limit: Trauma checks occur per 10 points; disorder thresholds are 40, 60, and 80.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.go_wrong: Failed Trauma Tests cause mental trauma; accumulated points bring permanent disorders.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.mind: The rules track and worsen mental damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.where_from: Horrific experiences and other causes of Insanity Points.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.combines: Degree of Madness modifies Trauma Tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.insanity-points-thres.blocked_reason: Point thresholds and triggered consequences are directly representable as rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.disorder-severity.name: Disorder severity

effect.summary: Minor, Severe, and Acute disorders change how often their effects occur and the modifier to resist them.

warhammer-40k.rule.disorder-severity.cost_or_limit: Minor grants +10 to resistance tests; Severe gives no modifier; Acute imposes –10.
warhammer-40k.rule.disorder-severity.mind: Controls the intensity of an existing disorder.
warhammer-40k.rule.disorder-severity.blocked_reason: Severity and test modifiers are straightforward game rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.name: Removing Insanity Points

effect.summary: With GM permission, a character may spend experience to reduce Insanity Points.

warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.cost_or_limit: Removing one point costs 100 XP; a character cannot drop a Degree of Madness or lose disorders.
warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.mind: Represents recovery through time and effort in play.
warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.where_from: In-game recovery and expenditure of experience.
warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.combines: Recovery may be represented by care, rest, faith, or penance.
warhammer-40k.rule.removing-insanity-poi.blocked_reason: A point cost and restriction on reducing a track are directly representable as rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.name: Corruption Point track

effect.summary: Corruption totals set a character’s corruption degree and the penalties for Malignancy Tests, with mutation tests at higher thresholds.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.cost_or_limit: Track bands are 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 91–99; 100 removes the character from play.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.go_wrong: Failed Malignancy Tests cause lasting metaphysical or psychosomatic scars; mutation may follow.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.mind: Corruption afflicts the character and can damage body and soul.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.who_may: Characters exposed to warp influence, dark rituals, cursed artifacts, or daemons.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.where_from: Chaos, warp exposure, forbidden knowledge, and related deeds.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.combines: Every 10 points prompts a Malignancy Test; Fear Rating and events can set gained points.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.mechanism: threshold-based corruption, malignancy, and mutation progression
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-point-trac.blocked_reason: The track explicitly models corruption of the soul and its escalating state, which the basic effect grammar cannot represent.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-and-mutati.name: Corruption and mutation resistance

effect.summary: At each 30 Corruption Points, test two Characteristics not previously used to resist mutation; failure on either brings one random Minor Mutation.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-and-mutati.cost_or_limit: Each Characteristic can be used only once for these tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-and-mutati.go_wrong: Failure on either test causes one mutation.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-and-mutati.who_may: Characters who reach the Corruption Point threshold
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-and-mutati.blocked_reason: The rule applies random, persistent character changes that the basic effect grammar cannot represent.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-governance-.name: Planetary governance and tithes

effect.summary: A hereditary Imperial Commander governs a planet in return for loyalty and regular tithes.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-governance-.cost_or_limit: The ruler owes loyalty and planetary tithes to the Emperor.
warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-governance-.blocked_reason: This is a governance mechanism, not an effect outside the basic grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-self-defenc.name: Planetary self-defence

effect.summary: Each planet must provide its own defences.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-self-defenc.cost_or_limit: Imperial Commanders are obliged to build ground defences, spaceports, and whatever defence fleets they can.
warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-self-defenc.combines: Imperial Navy ships may also be stationed in vulnerable systems.
warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-self-defenc.blocked_reason: This is a world-building rule rather than a power effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.low-gothic.name: Low Gothic

effect.summary: The common everyday language allows communication across much of the Imperium.

warhammer-40k.rule.low-gothic.cost_or_limit: Its dialects vary substantially between worlds and communities.
warhammer-40k.rule.low-gothic.combines: It is also called Base Gothic or Common Tongue.
warhammer-40k.rule.low-gothic.blocked_reason: Communication through a shared language is representable as information transfer.

warhammer-40k.rule.high-gothic.name: High Gothic

effect.summary: A stable formal language supports clear communication of complex ideas between educated speakers.

warhammer-40k.rule.high-gothic.cost_or_limit: It is mainly used in formal or precise exchanges.
warhammer-40k.rule.high-gothic.combines: Also known as Principal Gothic, Archaic Gothic, and Prime Gothic.
warhammer-40k.rule.high-gothic.blocked_reason: Communication through a shared language is representable as information transfer.

warhammer-40k.rule.techna-lingua.name: Techna-Lingua

effect.summary: The Mechanicus language communicates technical and order-specific knowledge.

warhammer-40k.rule.techna-lingua.cost_or_limit: Few outside the Priesthood of Mars can understand it fully; its phrases are treated as forbidden to the unsanctified.
warhammer-40k.rule.techna-lingua.who_may: Tech-Priests and those sanctified by the Machine God
warhammer-40k.rule.techna-lingua.combines: Some terms appear in technical or industrial Low Gothic.
warhammer-40k.rule.techna-lingua.blocked_reason: Communication through a language is representable as information transfer.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel.name: Warp travel

effect.summary: Warp engines carry ships through the warp, allowing them to re-emerge at a different real-space location.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel.cost_or_limit: Ordinary safe journeys use short jumps of roughly four or five light years; longer jumps are dangerous and unpredictable.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel.go_wrong: Ships may emerge far off course or be destroyed.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel.combines: Navigators can steer longer piloted journeys using warp currents and the Astronomican.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel.blocked_reason: The rule describes movement of a ship from one position to another.

warhammer-40k.rule.time-displacement.name: Time Displacement

effect.summary: Time passes at different and variable rates in real space and warp space.

warhammer-40k.rule.time-displacement.cost_or_limit: Crews cannot know the exact duration of a journey until it ends.
warhammer-40k.rule.time-displacement.combines: The differing rates make journey duration uncertain.
warhammer-40k.rule.time-displacement.blocked_reason: The basic grammar cannot model different time rates between locations.

warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.name: Calculated jump

effect.summary: A ship plots a warp course from observed currents without an onboard Navigator steering it.

warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.cost_or_limit: A calculated jump should not exceed four light years at once.
warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.go_wrong: Changing currents can make the ship go off course.
warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.where_from: Warp space, using observations from real space
warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.combines: The method assumes currents do not change significantly during the flight.
warhammer-40k.rule.calculated-jump.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a travel limit and a positional effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.name: Piloted jump

effect.summary: A Navigator steers a ship through warp space, correcting for changing currents.

warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.cost_or_limit: Most jumps cover no more than 5,000 light years, though longer ones have been made.
warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.go_wrong: Warp hazards and time variation remain possible.
warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.mind: The Navigator senses and responds to warp currents.
warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.combines: It relies on the Astronomican’s psychic beacon.
warhammer-40k.rule.piloted-jump.blocked_reason: The rule describes ship movement and a travel limit.

warhammer-40k.rule.warpstorms.name: Warpstorms

effect.summary: Warpstorms can obscure the Astronomican and isolate star systems.

warhammer-40k.rule.warpstorms.cost_or_limit: They can last for hundreds of years.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpstorms.go_wrong: Ships entering one may be destroyed or flung far off course.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpstorms.combines: They interfere with the Astronomican and warp travel.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpstorms.blocked_reason: The storm is a large-scale field that obstructs signals and makes travel hazardous.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-jump-point-restr.name: Warp jump-point restriction

effect.summary: Warp engines should only be activated beyond the system’s jump-point and ships should re-enter beyond the destination jump-point.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-jump-point-restr.cost_or_limit: Ships must cross the boundary where interplanetary debris falls below maximum warp density.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-jump-point-restr.go_wrong: Premature activation or re-entry can tear a ship apart or send it thousands of light years off course.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-jump-point-restr.combines: The restriction applies to entering and leaving warp space.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-jump-point-restr.blocked_reason: This is a clear travel restriction and consequence.

warhammer-40k.rule.warpspace-channels.name: Warpspace Channels

effect.summary: Established routes through the warp connect systems with relatively predictable travel.

warhammer-40k.rule.warpspace-channels.cost_or_limit: Long journeys and large fleets are harder to keep accurate and together.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpspace-channels.go_wrong: Warp currents can disperse fleets or send ships off course.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpspace-channels.combines: Channels are charted conduits used by much shipping.
warhammer-40k.rule.warpspace-channels.blocked_reason: This is a route modifier to ordinary ship movement.

warhammer-40k.rule.unregistered-ships-ar.name: Unregistered ships are assumed hostile

effect.summary: Naval forces may treat any ship lacking registration as hostile.

warhammer-40k.rule.unregistered-ships-ar.cost_or_limit: Unregistered vessels risk attack or destruction.
warhammer-40k.rule.unregistered-ships-ar.combines: Registration identifies ships and permits fleet administration.
warhammer-40k.rule.unregistered-ships-ar.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.navigatorless-warp-ju.name: Navigatorless warp-jump limit

effect.summary: Without a Navigator, a ship can jump no more than four light years at a time.

warhammer-40k.rule.navigatorless-warp-ju.cost_or_limit: The maximum jump is four light years, compared with 5,000 for a piloted jump.
warhammer-40k.rule.navigatorless-warp-ju.where_from: Warp-travel rules described for the Imperium.
warhammer-40k.rule.navigatorless-warp-ju.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.segmentae-registratio.name: Segmentae Registration

effect.summary: Interstellar ships must be registered to one or more Segmentae fleets to travel normally.

warhammer-40k.rule.segmentae-registratio.cost_or_limit: A ship needs special fleet permission to enter a Segmentum where it is not registered.
warhammer-40k.rule.segmentae-registratio.go_wrong: An unidentified unregistered vessel may be attacked or destroyed as hostile.
warhammer-40k.rule.segmentae-registratio.combines: Registration supports identification and records of shipping.
warhammer-40k.rule.segmentae-registratio.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.merchant-charter.name: Merchant Charter

effect.summary: Merchant ships serve a fleet under a charter that sets the captain’s authority and responsibilities.

warhammer-40k.rule.merchant-charter.cost_or_limit: Charters vary and require a sworn feudal oath entered in fleet records.
warhammer-40k.rule.merchant-charter.combines: Includes Fleet, Free, Hereditary, and Hereditary Free charters.
warhammer-40k.rule.merchant-charter.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.fleet-charter.name: Fleet Charter

effect.summary: A Fleet Captain serves fixed routes and may be removed from command or reassigned.

warhammer-40k.rule.fleet-charter.cost_or_limit: It is the least prestigious and least secure charter.
warhammer-40k.rule.fleet-charter.go_wrong: The captain may lose command and receive a shore posting.
warhammer-40k.rule.fleet-charter.combines: The captain is appointed similarly to a free captain but follows fixed routes.
warhammer-40k.rule.fleet-charter.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.free-charter.name: Free Charter

effect.summary: A fleet-appointed captain may trade freely within the fleet’s Segmentae, usually away from established routes.

warhammer-40k.rule.free-charter.cost_or_limit: The captain is generally forbidden to trade established routes.
warhammer-40k.rule.free-charter.combines: Often awarded to experienced fleet officials.
warhammer-40k.rule.free-charter.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-charter.name: Hereditary Charter

effect.summary: A captain may nominate a successor who inherits the ship and its route obligations after swearing allegiance.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-charter.cost_or_limit: The successor must carry cargo and passengers only on the inherited routes.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-charter.who_may: A Hereditary Captain and nominated successor.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-charter.combines: Transfers command by succession after death or retirement.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-charter.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-free-chart.name: Hereditary Free Charter

effect.summary: A hereditary captain may trade freely within the bounds of the fleet charter.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-free-chart.cost_or_limit: The captain’s authority remains limited by the charter and relevant Segmentae.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-free-chart.combines: May be registered in multiple Segmentae fleets.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-free-chart.mechanism: Hereditary command with broad trade permissions.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-free-chart.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.name: Civil fleet route licences

effect.summary: Privately owned interstellar ships need licensed routes, typically renewed every hundred years.

warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.cost_or_limit: Licences must be purchased and may expire during long voyages affected by time dilation.
warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.go_wrong: A licence may lapse before the ship completes its journey.
warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.who_may: Fleet authorities issue licences; civil fleets and private ships obtain them.
warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.combines: Licences may cover routes or single trips.
warhammer-40k.rule.civil-fleet-route-lic.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.name: Spaceship longevity

effect.summary: Ships can remain in service for centuries or millennia through continuous repair, refitting, and reconstruction.

warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.cost_or_limit: They require extensive maintenance crews and material resources.
warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.go_wrong: Battle damage, asteroids, warp exposure, and component wear continually degrade ships.
warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.who_may: Ship crews and maintenance workers sustain vessels.
warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.combines: Onboard workshops, factories, and refineries support repairs.
warhammer-40k.rule.spaceship-longevity.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-jump-point.name: Warp-drive jump point restriction

effect.summary: Ships must reach a safe point at the edge of a system before activating warp drives.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-jump-point.cost_or_limit: Engaging a warp drive inside a star system is catastrophic.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-jump-point.go_wrong: The ship may be torn apart and the system’s planets and population endangered.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-jump-point.combines: Plasma drives carry ships to the jump point before being disengaged.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-drive-jump-point.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.name: Warrant of Trade authority

effect.summary: The warrant permits Rogue Traders to cross Imperial borders and deal with outsiders despite general prohibitions.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.cost_or_limit: Authority is granted by the Imperium and does not provide unlimited freedom within Imperial space.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.go_wrong: Returning to Imperial space and acting beyond authority can attract official attention.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.where_from: Imperial law and High Lords’ sanction.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.combines: May be paired with military resources from the Imperium or investors.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.mechanism: Legal exception to the restriction on dealings with outsiders.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-of-trade-auth.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.name: Rogue Trader backing

effect.summary: A Rogue Trader supported by investors may owe them a portion of the expedition’s profits.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.cost_or_limit: The obligation depends on the backing arrangement.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.go_wrong: A trader who abandons the obligation may face capture rewards.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.who_may: Rogue Traders with investors or other backers.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.combines: Backers may provide military resources in expectation of profit.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-backing.blocked_reason: This is a world rule rather than a character effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-rights-beyond.name: Warrant rights beyond Imperial borders

effect.summary: A Rogue Trader may claim worlds and privileges by conquest or other chosen means.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-rights-beyond.cost_or_limit: The passage describes the broadest authority beyond Imperial borders.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-rights-beyond.combines: Can support conquest, colonisation, or exclusive trade arrangements.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-rights-beyond.blocked_reason: This is a rule about legal permissions, not a direct game effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-rogue-trad.name: Hereditary Rogue Trader Warrants

effect.summary: A Warrant passes from one generation to the next while heirs remain.

warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-rogue-trad.cost_or_limit: The line ends if there are no surviving heirs.
warhammer-40k.rule.hereditary-rogue-trad.blocked_reason: This is a succession rule and needs no effect beyond tracking inheritance.

warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.name: Finite forces beyond the Imperium

effect.summary: A Rogue Trader operating far from Imperial support must husband troops because losses are hard to replace.

warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.cost_or_limit: Replenishment may require recruiting from conquered worlds or demanding local service.
warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.go_wrong: A force can be exhausted through casualties.
warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.who_may: Rogue Traders commanding ground forces beyond Imperial reach.
warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.combines: Local feudal service, coerced recruitment, and alien auxiliaries may offset losses.
warhammer-40k.rule.finite-forces-beyond-.blocked_reason: This is a resource limit that can be tracked directly in play.

warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.name: Temporary attachments of Imperial Guard

effect.summary: Guard regiments assigned to a Rogue Trader are nominally temporary, but often remain with the expedition permanently.

warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.cost_or_limit: Their return is unlikely, especially after surviving frontier conflicts.
warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.go_wrong: The force may be lost in combat.
warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.who_may: Imperial Guard regiments seconded to Rogue Traders.
warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.combines: May accompany a fleet with auxiliary units and advisors.
warhammer-40k.rule.temporary-attachments.blocked_reason: This rule can be handled by tracking a force's assignment and availability.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-obligations.name: Warrant obligations

effect.summary: A Warrant may require service, intervention, settlement, reclamation, or exploration.

warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-obligations.cost_or_limit: The holder must fulfil its attached conditions.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-obligations.go_wrong: Failure may bring Imperial enforcement or forfeiture.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-obligations.combines: Compliance may be ensured with agents, force, incentives, or assassins.
warhammer-40k.rule.warrant-obligations.blocked_reason: The rule is a persistent obligation that can be tracked directly.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.name: Rogue Trader inheritance

effect.summary: A Warrant may be inherited, with authority concentrated in the line’s titular head.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.cost_or_limit: Competing heirs may struggle for leadership.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.go_wrong: Strife, intimidation, or assassination may occur.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.where_from: The lineage of a Warrant-holding house.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.combines: A line may continue across generations.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-inherita.blocked_reason: The succession of a persistent authority between characters is not covered by the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.name: Revocation and forfeiture

effect.summary: Revocation permanently removes a line’s Warrant powers and privileges.

warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.cost_or_limit: Authorities may revoke a Warrant when a Rogue Trader’s actions exceed acceptable bounds.
warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.go_wrong: The line loses its powers and privileges, though it may survive in diminished form.
warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.who_may: Imperial authorities can revoke; affected Rogue Trader lines lose the grant.
warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.combines: A severe response may follow betrayal or acting against Imperial interests.
warhammer-40k.rule.revocation-and-forfei.blocked_reason: The lasting revocation and loss of an inherited grant require explicit authority-state handling.

warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.name: Imperial compliance contingencies

effect.summary: The Imperium may use representatives, force, rewards, agents, or assassins to secure compliance.

warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.cost_or_limit: Contingencies vary by voyage and warrant conditions.
warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.go_wrong: Noncompliance or betrayal may trigger coercive action.
warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.where_from: Arrangements made before or during a Rogue Trader voyage.
warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.combines: May include attached forces, replenishment promises, crew agents, or assassins.
warhammer-40k.rule.imperial-compliance-c.blocked_reason: These are enforceable conditions and consequences that can be tracked directly.

warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.name: Maw navigation risk

effect.summary: The storms make crossing nearly impossible except along rare stable routes.

warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.cost_or_limit: Navigators depend on skill and scant information.
warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.go_wrong: A sudden storm surge can mislead or destroy a vessel.
warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.mind: The warp’s dangers may imperil a Navigator’s soul.
warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.combines: The Koronus Passage is the greatest navigable route described.
warhammer-40k.rule.maw-navigation-risk.blocked_reason: The restriction concerns persistent environmental effects across a broad region.

warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.name: Stations of Passage safety

effect.summary: Ships may safely drop from the warp at designated real-space stations while crossing the Maw.

warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.cost_or_limit: Safety applies at specific locations, some of which are avoided.
warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.go_wrong: Unexpected upheaval in the warp may still require refuge.
warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.combines: Some stations also serve as refuges or covert meeting places.
warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.mechanism: Designated safe points for warp exit.
warhammer-40k.rule.stations-of-passage-s.blocked_reason: The rule identifies where a travel procedure can safely occur.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-thousand-charts.name: The Thousand Charts

effect.summary: Charts of the region often contradict each other; some may mislead, and a correct cipher may reconcile them.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-thousand-charts.cost_or_limit: Navigation records are unreliable and may be dangerous to follow.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-thousand-charts.go_wrong: A false route can lure explorers to destruction.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-thousand-charts.combines: Charts may combine with a cipher to disclose further information.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-to-the-storm.name: Lost to the Storm

effect.summary: Local warp phenomena divert ships, immobilize them, and make established routes vanish or lead elsewhere.

warhammer-40k.rule.lost-to-the-storm.cost_or_limit: Even charted routes may be unreliable.
warhammer-40k.rule.lost-to-the-storm.go_wrong: Ships can be lost or their Gellar Fields attacked by tempests.

warhammer-40k.rule.waaagh-is-gathering.name: Waaagh! is gathering

effect.summary: The Orks are collectively assembling for a destructive campaign awaiting a dominant boss.

warhammer-40k.rule.waaagh-is-gathering.cost_or_limit: Its emergence depends on an undisputed leader arising from internal conflict.
warhammer-40k.rule.waaagh-is-gathering.go_wrong: If unchecked, the resulting Waaagh! will devastate the Expanse and beyond.
warhammer-40k.rule.waaagh-is-gathering.mind: Orks feel an instinctive drive to gather.
warhammer-40k.rule.waaagh-is-gathering.combines: Boss dominance and inter-Ork warfare drive the gathering.

warhammer-40k.rule.chaos-worship-forfeit.name: Chaos worship forfeits the soul

effect.summary: Those enthralled by Chaos lose their immortal souls and become subject to their masters.

warhammer-40k.rule.chaos-worship-forfeit.cost_or_limit: Applies to those who become enthralled to Chaos.
warhammer-40k.rule.chaos-worship-forfeit.go_wrong: Eternal damnation and loss of agency
warhammer-40k.rule.chaos-worship-forfeit.mind: Subject to the whims of dark masters
warhammer-40k.rule.chaos-worship-forfeit.blocked_reason: The rule changes the fate and ownership of a soul, which the basic effect grammar cannot model.

warhammer-40k.rule.webway-travel.name: Webway travel

effect.summary: Travelers enter a portal, cross stable passages, and exit through another portal, shortening interstellar journeys.

warhammer-40k.rule.webway-travel.go_wrong: Unlike warp voyages, passages avoid ordinary warp dangers.
warhammer-40k.rule.webway-travel.who_may: Living creatures and vehicles that fit the portals
warhammer-40k.rule.webway-travel.combines: Connects locations through stable warp tunnels.
warhammer-40k.rule.webway-travel.blocked_reason: The basic grammar cannot model passage through spatial tunnels and portal-linked destinations.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-eldar-path.name: The Eldar Path

effect.summary: A chosen Path places bounds on an Eldar's experiences.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-eldar-path.cost_or_limit: Leaving the Path increases vulnerability to the Eldar nemesis and loss of self.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-eldar-path.go_wrong: Outcasts may be consumed by their experiences.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-eldar-path.blocked_reason: The rule requires persistent mental constraint and risk of losing oneself.

warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.name: Halo Artefact bonding corrupts the bearer

effect.summary: Bonding gradually turns a bearer into an undying, inhuman monster.

warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.cost_or_limit: The bearer is physically bonded to the device.
warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.go_wrong: Body, mind, and soul are corrupted; unnatural thirsts and nightmares take hold.
warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.who_may: Those who meld with Halo Artefacts
warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.combines: Some devices also halt aging or grant other powers.
warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.mechanism: Progressive item-linked bodily and mental corruption
warhammer-40k.rule.halo-artefact-bonding.blocked_reason: The rule combines a bonded item's power with gradual transformation and mental corruption.

warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation-.name: Daemon manifestation and persistence

effect.summary: Daemons are made from the Warp and cannot readily persist in the material universe without bloodshed, misery and death.

warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation-.cost_or_limit: Material-world persistence depends on bloodshed, misery and death.
warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation-.go_wrong: Without those conditions, a daemon cannot readily maintain its hold on the universe.
warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation-.blocked_reason: The passage gives a supernatural persistence condition but does not provide a basic effect for daemon existence.

warhammer-40k.rule.profit-threshold-for-.name: Profit threshold for Imperial records

effect.summary: The Explorers need Profit of at least 45 to impress record-holding authorities and obtain the location of Magoros.

warhammer-40k.rule.profit-threshold-for-.go_wrong: Below the threshold, this route does not provide the location.
warhammer-40k.rule.profit-threshold-for-.who_may: Explorers petitioning the Navy or Administratum
warhammer-40k.rule.profit-threshold-for-.combines: Used to obtain records about the Expanse.
warhammer-40k.rule.profit-threshold-for-.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward threshold requirement.

effect.summary: Waiting for an eddy costs several days and reduces ship Morale by 1d5.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.name: Warp eddy exposure

effect.summary: Failed navigation tests expose Explorers to warp miasma that impairs WS and BS tests for 1d5 days.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.cost_or_limit: Piloter and Navigator each test Perception at Difficult (–10); Explorers test Willpower at Challenging (+0).
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.go_wrong: Failure brings warp exposure and temporary combat penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.mind: Failed Willpower tests bring nauseating visions and lethargy.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.who_may: Ships pressing through the eddy and their Explorers.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.where_from: Warp energy soaking into the vessel.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-eddy-exposure.combines: Both piloting and Navigator tests must be passed to plot a safe path.

warhammer-40k.rule.debris-field-manoeuvr.name: Debris-field manoeuvres

effect.summary: Manoeuvres in the debris field have their difficulty increased by one step.

warhammer-40k.rule.debris-field-manoeuvr.cost_or_limit: Applies to all manoeuvres in the field.
warhammer-40k.rule.debris-field-manoeuvr.go_wrong: Failed tests may trigger the ordinary asteroid-field consequences.
warhammer-40k.rule.debris-field-manoeuvr.where_from: The debris field around the pirate ambush.
warhammer-40k.rule.debris-field-manoeuvr.combines: Several especially dense areas also use asteroid-field effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.magoros-radiation-pul.name: Magoros radiation pulse

effect.summary: The star’s radiation pulse briefly blinds sensors and ripples through void shields.

warhammer-40k.rule.magoros-radiation-pul.cost_or_limit: Occurs every 102 minutes and lasts about 58 seconds.
warhammer-40k.rule.magoros-radiation-pul.go_wrong: People exposed without a vessel or atmosphere risk fatal radiation exposure.
warhammer-40k.rule.magoros-radiation-pul.who_may: Ships and people in the system.
warhammer-40k.rule.magoros-radiation-pul.combines: Can conceal attacks or interrupt contact.

warhammer-40k.rule.righteous-path-energy.name: Righteous Path energy seals

effect.summary: Energy seals prevent access to the ship’s core until disabled.

warhammer-40k.rule.righteous-path-energy.cost_or_limit: They can be cut through with heavy equipment or controlled from the bridge.
warhammer-40k.rule.righteous-path-energy.who_may: Those with access to the bridge control or appropriate equipment.
warhammer-40k.rule.righteous-path-energy.combines: The seals are linked directly to the bridge.
warhammer-40k.rule.righteous-path-energy.blocked_reason: A reusable containment or seal-disabling mechanism is not part of the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-tides.name: Gravity Tides

effect.summary: Gravitational fields in affected regions churn and may hinder or assist travel.

warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-tides.cost_or_limit: Some tides require difficult piloting tests to enter orbit; orbiting ships need repeated tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-tides.who_may: Applies to vessels in affected systems.
warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-tides.combines: May create riptides or helpful currents.
warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-tides.blocked_reason: The effect is a localized force hazard with stated travel consequences.

warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.name: Ill-Omened

effect.summary: A system’s malign reputation can worsen morale, fear, and other outcomes.

warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.cost_or_limit: Entry can cost morale; fear tests and other checks may suffer penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.go_wrong: Some optional effects can nullify a Fate Point or increase Insanity gains.
warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.who_may: Applies to crews and explorers in the system.
warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.combines: May also impose Willpower or Divination-related penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.ill-omened.blocked_reason: The passage specifies several different accumulating penalties and conditional misfortunes.

warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.name: Stellar Anomaly

effect.summary: An anomaly reduces planetary formation, aids local navigation, and changes Warp travel hazards.

warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.cost_or_limit: Systems generate fewer planets; Warp encounter checks are less frequent.
warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.go_wrong: Realspace hazards replace ordinary results on doubles.
warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.who_may: Applies to ships navigating the system.
warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.combines: Realspace hazards may resemble gravity riptides, radiation bursts, or solar flares.
warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.mechanism: Massive celestial body alters system formation and travel
warhammer-40k.rule.stellar-anomaly.blocked_reason: Its effects are changes to generation and travel checks, not an unsupported basic effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.name: Warp Stasis

effect.summary: Warp currents slow travel into and out of the affected system.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.cost_or_limit: Travel time and astropathic messaging time are doubled; coherent messages suffer a Psy Rating penalty.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.go_wrong: A ship may be left becalmed and unable to reach realspace safely.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.mind: Psychic users may face penalties and altered phenomena.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.who_may: Applies to ships and psykers in the system.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.combines: Optional effects hinder psychic tests and prevent Push-level techniques.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-stasis.blocked_reason: The rule modifies psychic abilities and phenomena beyond the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.name: Warp Turbulence

effect.summary: Unstable Warp currents make travel and psychic activity more dangerous.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.cost_or_limit: Navigators suffer a penalty on Warp navigation tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.go_wrong: Psychic phenomena and Corruption may increase; a planet may be cut off by a permanent storm.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.mind: Psychic techniques may gain power but are riskier.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.who_may: Applies to Navigators, psykers, and ships in the system.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.combines: Can affect Warp jumps, psychic phenomena, Corruption, and access to a planet.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-turbulence.blocked_reason: It alters psychic technique strength and multiple psychic and travel outcomes.

warhammer-40k.rule.asteroid-belt.name: Asteroid Belt

effect.summary: A debris ring obstructs direct passage through the system’s orbital plane.

warhammer-40k.rule.asteroid-belt.cost_or_limit: Passing through requires navigation; bypassing it adds travel time.
warhammer-40k.rule.asteroid-belt.go_wrong: Poor navigation risks collision with debris.
warhammer-40k.rule.asteroid-belt.who_may: Applies to ships crossing the belt.
warhammer-40k.rule.asteroid-belt.blocked_reason: The belt is a navigable obstruction with stated alternatives.

warhammer-40k.rule.derelict-station-dama.name: Derelict Station damage profile

effect.summary: When fired upon in ship combat or damaged collaterally, a derelict station has 10 Armour and 4d10 Hull Integrity, with no other defences.

warhammer-40k.rule.derelict-station-dama.who_may: Applies when the station is damaged in the stated circumstances.
warhammer-40k.rule.derelict-station-dama.blocked_reason: This is a direct rule for assigning defensive statistics.

warhammer-40k.rule.dust-clouds-follow-ne.name: Dust Clouds follow Nebula rules

effect.summary: Dust Clouds use the Nebula rules in the Rogue Trader Core Rulebook.

warhammer-40k.rule.dust-clouds-follow-ne.cost_or_limit: Smaller temporary clouds do not count as generated System Elements.
warhammer-40k.rule.dust-clouds-follow-ne.blocked_reason: The referenced Nebula mechanics are not included in this passage.

warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-riptides-foll.name: Gravity Riptides follow Gravity Tide rules

effect.summary: Gravity Riptides use the Gravity Tides rules in the Rogue Trader Core Rulebook.

warhammer-40k.rule.gravity-riptides-foll.blocked_reason: The referenced Gravity Tides mechanics are not included here.

warhammer-40k.rule.solar-zone-climate-li.name: Solar Zone climate limits

effect.summary: A planet without atmosphere is Burning in the Inner Cauldron and Ice in the Outer Reaches; atmospheric planets adjust their climate roll by zone.

warhammer-40k.rule.solar-zone-climate-li.cost_or_limit: Apply –6 in the Inner Cauldron and +6 in the Outer Reaches; Primary Biosphere airless worlds may be either extreme.
warhammer-40k.rule.solar-zone-climate-li.combines: Depends on Solar Zone and atmosphere.
warhammer-40k.rule.solar-zone-climate-li.blocked_reason: This is a direct planetary generation rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.habitability-generati.name: Habitability generation limits

effect.summary: Habitability is not rolled for airless worlds or atmospheres other than Tainted or Pure; cold and hot worlds take penalties, and Burning or Ice worlds are heavily capped.

warhammer-40k.rule.habitability-generati.cost_or_limit: Hot and Cold worlds take –2; Burning and Ice worlds take –7 and cannot exceed result 3.
warhammer-40k.rule.habitability-generati.combines: At GM discretion, otherwise unsuitable worlds may still roll and host adapted life.
warhammer-40k.rule.habitability-generati.blocked_reason: This is a direct rule for a generation roll.

warhammer-40k.rule.hostile-native-life.name: Hostile native life

effect.summary: Life adapted to a hostile atmosphere or climate cannot survive on normally habitable planets, which remain hazardous to outsiders.

warhammer-40k.rule.hostile-native-life.cost_or_limit: Applies when a hostile world receives Limited Ecosystem or Verdant habitability.
warhammer-40k.rule.hostile-native-life.who_may: Native life and non-native organisms on such planets.
warhammer-40k.rule.hostile-native-life.combines: May apply when the GM permits a habitability roll despite unsuitable conditions.
warhammer-40k.rule.hostile-native-life.blocked_reason: This is a direct survival restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.landmass-generation.name: Landmass generation

effect.summary: Planets roll 1d10 for separate landmasses; those with abundant liquid water use a lower threshold.

warhammer-40k.rule.landmass-generation.cost_or_limit: A result of 8+ normally gives multiple landmasses; with abundant liquid water, 4+ suffices; separate landmasses have 1d5 major regions.
warhammer-40k.rule.landmass-generation.combines: Water availability changes the roll threshold.
warhammer-40k.rule.landmass-generation.blocked_reason: This is a direct generation procedure.

warhammer-40k.rule.territory-generation-.name: Territory generation limits

effect.summary: Territory count depends on Body and Habitability; worlds below Limited Ecosystem normally do not generate territories randomly.
