warhammer-40k.rule.territory-generation-.cost_or_limit: Roll 1d5 and apply the table’s modifiers; territories get a base terrain and 1d5–2 traits, minimum one.
warhammer-40k.rule.territory-generation-.combines: The GM may choose suitable territories for otherwise ineligible planets.
warhammer-40k.rule.territory-generation-.blocked_reason: This is a direct environment-generation procedure.

warhammer-40k.rule.duplicate-territory-t.name: Duplicate Territory Traits

effect.summary: Repeated traits multiply their mechanical effects unless that is illogical, in which case the GM may reroll, replace, or ignore duplicates.

warhammer-40k.rule.duplicate-territory-t.who_may: Applies to Territories with repeated traits.
warhammer-40k.rule.duplicate-territory-t.blocked_reason: This is a direct rule for combining repeated effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.name: Resource Abundance and depletion

effect.summary: Mining ventures and colonies reduce a resource’s Abundance as it is converted into Achievement Points or Profit Factor.

warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.cost_or_limit: Depletion amount depends on Endeavour scope and the resource-depletion table.
warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.go_wrong: A resource may be exhausted by exploitation.
warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.who_may: Explorers and their colonies exploiting resources.
warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.combines: Uses Endeavour rules to determine rewards.
warhammer-40k.rule.resource-abundance-an.blocked_reason: This is a direct resource economy rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.name: Archeotech Cache discoveries deplete abundance

effect.summary: Each discovered item reduces cache Abundance by 2, while each Voidship Component reduces it by 10.

warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.cost_or_limit: The cache yields 1d5+1 items per specific manifestation.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.go_wrong: The Adeptus Mechanicus may claim discoveries made by a colony.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.who_may: Applies to Explorers finding cache items.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.combines: Items are generated using the Treasure Generator with Archeotech selected as origin.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-cache-disc.blocked_reason: This is a direct rule for generating discoveries and reducing a resource.

warhammer-40k.rule.resource-varieties-ha.name: Resource varieties have no explicit mechanical differences

effect.summary: Different mineral resource types are handled mechanically the same, though their narrative and trade details may shape Endeavours or negotiations.

warhammer-40k.rule.resource-varieties-ha.combines: The GM may use resource details when designing commercial interactions.
warhammer-40k.rule.resource-varieties-ha.blocked_reason: This is a direct rule that resource varieties share mechanics.

warhammer-40k.rule.organic-compound-harv.name: Organic Compound harvesting

effect.summary: Harvesting depletes the resource’s abundance.

warhammer-40k.rule.organic-compound-harv.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward depletion and colony-output adjustment.

warhammer-40k.rule.conservative-organic-.name: Conservative Organic Compound harvesting

effect.summary: Harvesting slows depletion in exchange for lower colony profit.

warhammer-40k.rule.conservative-organic-.cost_or_limit: Profit Factor falls by 2; yearly depletion falls by 1d10, to a minimum of zero.
warhammer-40k.rule.conservative-organic-.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a numerical cost and depletion change.

warhammer-40k.rule.unprepared-curative-a.name: Unprepared Curative application

effect.summary: Rushed treatment can restore a small amount of health or remove critical damage.

warhammer-40k.rule.unprepared-curative-a.cost_or_limit: Medicae Tests take a –40 penalty; success has only minor effects, restoring 1d5 Wounds or removing one Critical Damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.unprepared-curative-a.go_wrong: May inflict Corruption or Insanity Points.
warhammer-40k.rule.unprepared-curative-a.blocked_reason: The treatment and its possible adverse effects are directly specified.

warhammer-40k.rule.juvenat-compound-proc.name: Juvenat Compound processing

effect.summary: Juvenat compounds require processing before they can be used safely.

warhammer-40k.rule.juvenat-compound-proc.cost_or_limit: Processing requires an appropriate, rare facility; basic analysis can usually identify potential.
warhammer-40k.rule.juvenat-compound-proc.go_wrong: Raw material is generally toxic or otherwise dangerous.
warhammer-40k.rule.juvenat-compound-proc.who_may: Those with access to a suitable facility
warhammer-40k.rule.juvenat-compound-proc.blocked_reason: This is a clear processing restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.harvesting-ill-omened.name: Harvesting ill-omened Xenos Ruins

effect.summary: Harvesting certain ruins reduces colony Complacency and Order each cycle.

warhammer-40k.rule.harvesting-ill-omened.cost_or_limit: Each 90-day harvesting cycle costs 1 Complacency and 1 Order.
warhammer-40k.rule.harvesting-ill-omened.go_wrong: At zero or less in either characteristic, the colony falls into madness and slaughter.
warhammer-40k.rule.harvesting-ill-omened.who_may: Colonies harvesting especially ill-omened sites, notably Yu’Vath ruins
warhammer-40k.rule.harvesting-ill-omened.blocked_reason: The rule tracks worsening colony characteristics over repeated cycles and a catastrophic threshold.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-landmark-ge.name: Planetary Landmark generation

effect.summary: A planet’s body determines how many Landmarks each Territory receives.

warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-landmark-ge.cost_or_limit: Small planets get 1d5 per Territory, Large 1d5+2, Vast 1d5+3; invalid Exceptional results are rerolled.
warhammer-40k.rule.planetary-landmark-ge.blocked_reason: The procedure is a simple count and selection rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.cave-network-navigati.name: Cave Network navigation exception

effect.summary: A scanner may let explorers navigate using a Cave Network as a reference point.

warhammer-40k.rule.cave-network-navigati.cost_or_limit: Requires GM approval and suitable scanning technology.
warhammer-40k.rule.cave-network-navigati.go_wrong: Without that aid, Cave Networks cannot normally provide the navigation benefit.
warhammer-40k.rule.cave-network-navigati.who_may: Explorers using a scanner or similar technology
warhammer-40k.rule.cave-network-navigati.blocked_reason: The exception specifies a condition for using the ordinary navigation bonus.

warhammer-40k.rule.mountain-navigation-b.name: Mountain navigation bonus

effect.summary: Mountains provide an additional navigation bonus when used as a reference.

warhammer-40k.rule.mountain-navigation-b.cost_or_limit: +10 to Navigate (Surface) in addition to the Landmark bonus.
warhammer-40k.rule.mountain-navigation-b.who_may: Explorers navigating with a Mountain reference
warhammer-40k.rule.mountain-navigation-b.combines: Stacks with the general Landmark bonus.
warhammer-40k.rule.mountain-navigation-b.blocked_reason: The bonus is a defined numerical modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.perpetual-storm-restr.name: Perpetual Storm restrictions

effect.summary: Only sufficiently substantial atmospheres support Perpetual Storms.

warhammer-40k.rule.perpetual-storm-restr.cost_or_limit: The planet must have a Moderate or Heavy atmosphere.
warhammer-40k.rule.perpetual-storm-restr.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward world-condition restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.reef-and-whirlpool-el.name: Reef and Whirlpool eligibility

effect.summary: These oceanic Landmarks normally require suitable water-bearing habitability.

warhammer-40k.rule.reef-and-whirlpool-el.cost_or_limit: Requires Liquid Water, Limited Ecosystem, or Verdant; Whirlpools rarely occur without two tide-affecting orbital features.
warhammer-40k.rule.reef-and-whirlpool-el.combines: GM may allow fossil reefs on dry planets.
warhammer-40k.rule.reef-and-whirlpool-el.blocked_reason: The rule specifies when the Landmark can be generated.

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.name: Creature generation for Limited Ecosystem worlds

effect.summary: A game master may generate up to six notable species for a Limited Ecosystem planet.

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.cost_or_limit: Up to six examples at GM discretion.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.combines: Uses Bestial Archetypes and Bestial Natures.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.blocked_reason: The rule is a simple limit on generated examples.

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.name: Creature generation for Verdant worlds

effect.summary: A Verdant planet should have at least one generated notable species.

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.cost_or_limit: Generate several more if explorers will spend substantial time in the wilds; a suggested minimum is one unique beast per major journey leg.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-generation-f.blocked_reason: The rule sets a direct baseline for notable creatures.

warhammer-40k.rule.random-bestial-archet.name: Random Bestial Archetype and Nature generation

effect.summary: Each randomly generated creature receives an archetype and at least one matching nature.

warhammer-40k.rule.random-bestial-archet.cost_or_limit: Roll once on each relevant table; more than one nature may be used.
warhammer-40k.rule.random-bestial-archet.combines: Additional archetypes or natures may be mixed at GM discretion.
warhammer-40k.rule.random-bestial-archet.blocked_reason: This is a creature-building procedure with defined selection steps.

warhammer-40k.rule.ptera-beast-flight-re.name: Ptera-Beast flight requirements

effect.summary: Large flying creatures are rare because flight becomes increasingly difficult as creatures grow.

warhammer-40k.rule.ptera-beast-flight-re.cost_or_limit: Species generally need unusual adaptations to support great size and flight.
warhammer-40k.rule.ptera-beast-flight-re.combines: Possible adaptations include gas sacs, metabolism, thermal lift, or stranger means.
warhammer-40k.rule.ptera-beast-flight-re.blocked_reason: This is a worldbuilding constraint rather than a runnable effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-habitat-adap.name: Creature habitat adaptation

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.creature-habitat-adap.cost_or_limit: Habitat-adapted creatures should have Resistance (Heat) and Resistance (Cold), plus other survival Talents or Skills they require.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-habitat-adap.go_wrong: Major recent environmental upheaval may make the usual adaptation inappropriate.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-habitat-adap.combines: Additional Skills and Talents may be required by the environment.
warhammer-40k.rule.creature-habitat-adap.blocked_reason: This is a rule governing creature capabilities, not a new game effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.name: Regional variant adjustment

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.cost_or_limit: Variants can change Skill Mastery by up to two steps, add or remove a few appropriate Talents, and in drastic cases adjust temperature tolerance by one step or alter specified Characteristics. Size usually stays unchanged.
warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.go_wrong: Changes too extreme for a variant should be generated as a separate species.
warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.where_from: Adaptation to a different region or habitat
warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.combines: May replace capabilities suited to the original habitat.
warhammer-40k.rule.regional-variant-adju.blocked_reason: The passage describes adjustments to existing traits and skills.

warhammer-40k.rule.native-sentient-popul.name: Native sentient population generation

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.native-sentient-popul.cost_or_limit: On a robust, habitable world, a 1d10 result of 8 or more gives a native sentient population; a normally uninhabitable world requires a 10, representing colonists or holdouts.
warhammer-40k.rule.native-sentient-popul.go_wrong: Multiple incompatible populations may need to be ignored or revised for coherence.
warhammer-40k.rule.native-sentient-popul.combines: Population type and development are rolled on the listed inhabitant tables.
warhammer-40k.rule.native-sentient-popul.blocked_reason: This is a generation procedure rather than a supernatural effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.development-resource-.name: Development resource consumption

effect.summary: Development can reduce a planet’s resource abundance.

warhammer-40k.rule.development-resource-.cost_or_limit: The text gives distinct resource reductions for development levels; exhausting a Minimal resource takes an extra step, and resources absent from a planet are treated as already spent.
warhammer-40k.rule.development-resource-.go_wrong: A population may exhaust its resources and become desperate for opportunities.
warhammer-40k.rule.development-resource-.combines: The amount and affected deposits vary by development level.
warhammer-40k.rule.development-resource-.blocked_reason: The rule changes resource abundance, which the basic effect grammar cannot quantify as a world-resource rating.

warhammer-40k.rule.development-classific.name: Development classification

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.development-classific.cost_or_limit: Development categories classify technological limits, not cultural sophistication; Colony and Orbital Habitation are special cases.
warhammer-40k.rule.development-classific.who_may: Civilisations assessed by Rogue Traders or GMs
warhammer-40k.rule.development-classific.combines: Categories include Primitive Clans, Pre-Industrial, Basic Industry, Advanced Industry, Colony, Orbital Habitation, and Voidfarers.
warhammer-40k.rule.development-classific.blocked_reason: This is a setting classification, not an effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.colony-development-li.name: Colony development limit

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.colony-development-li.cost_or_limit: A Colony’s advanced equipment is inherited or supplied from elsewhere; its industry mainly maintains it. Self-sufficiency or independence moves it to another Development level.
warhammer-40k.rule.colony-development-li.combines: May possess technology beyond its own production capabilities.
warhammer-40k.rule.colony-development-li.blocked_reason: This is a rule defining a civilisation’s development status.

warhammer-40k.rule.orbital-habitation-re.name: Orbital Habitation resource rule

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.orbital-habitation-re.cost_or_limit: Orbital Habitation leaves the planet’s resources completely unaffected.
warhammer-40k.rule.orbital-habitation-re.where_from: Living in stations above a planet
warhammer-40k.rule.orbital-habitation-re.combines: A population may still mine asteroids or possess defensive capabilities.
warhammer-40k.rule.orbital-habitation-re.blocked_reason: This is a direct restriction on resource depletion.

warhammer-40k.rule.primitive-weapon-qual.name: Primitive weapon quality

effect.summary: none

warhammer-40k.rule.primitive-weapon-qual.cost_or_limit: Weapons and armour made by Pre-Industrial societies have the Primitive Quality; the passage also assigns it to Basic Industry and Primitive Clans output.
warhammer-40k.rule.primitive-weapon-qual.who_may: Weapons and armour produced at the stated Development levels
warhammer-40k.rule.primitive-weapon-qual.combines: Advanced Industry equipment may also have this quality.
warhammer-40k.rule.primitive-weapon-qual.blocked_reason: This is a quality rule; no particular effect is given here.

warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-maiden-world-te.name: Eldar Maiden World terraforming

effect.summary: Eldar terraforming can make a habitable world Verdant and increase its Organic Compound resource abundance.

warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-maiden-world-te.cost_or_limit: At the GM’s discretion; abundance increases by 2d10.
warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-maiden-world-te.go_wrong: Explorers’ Endeavours involving a Maiden World trigger a Misfortune on a 1d10 result of 7 or more, possibly before arrival.
warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-maiden-world-te.combines: The Misfortune reflects Eldar retaliation and may be guided by Farseers.
warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-maiden-world-te.blocked_reason: The rule requires a probabilistic Misfortune trigger whose timing can precede the relevant Endeavour.

warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-webway-reinforc.name: Eldar webway reinforcement

effect.summary: Hidden gates can let Eldar reinforcements emerge unexpectedly.

warhammer-40k.rule.eldar-webway-reinforc.blocked_reason: The passage implies transport through a networked space but the basic grammar cannot model the Webway’s spatial connection.

warhammer-40k.rule.severian-s-postulate.name: Severian’s Postulate

effect.summary: Ork spores drift through space, fall on worlds, and can establish populations when enough survive together.

warhammer-40k.rule.severian-s-postulate.cost_or_limit: Most spores burn up on re-entry or become inert when isolated from Orks.
warhammer-40k.rule.severian-s-postulate.where_from: Observations by Magos Severian, an Explorator.
warhammer-40k.rule.severian-s-postulate.blocked_reason: This describes a natural propagation mechanism.

warhammer-40k.rule.ork-voidfarer-resourc.name: Ork Voidfarer resource depletion

effect.summary: Ork Voidfarers consume all resource types without depleting them beyond the usual amount for their development.

warhammer-40k.rule.ork-voidfarer-resourc.cost_or_limit: Territories are wasteland with the Ruined Territory Trait on a 1d10 result of 4 or higher; all resource abundance falls by 1d10+5.
warhammer-40k.rule.ork-voidfarer-resourc.blocked_reason: This is a game-world resource mechanism.

warhammer-40k.rule.peace-with-orks.name: Peace with Orks

effect.summary: Orks cannot understand peace, and encounters with them invariably lead to conflict.

warhammer-40k.rule.peace-with-orks.mind: Orks lack the concept of peace.
warhammer-40k.rule.peace-with-orks.combines: Ork aggression also applies to other Orks.
warhammer-40k.rule.peace-with-orks.blocked_reason: This is a social rule rather than a power effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.name: Rak’Gol Rad-Zones

effect.summary: Rak’Gol settlements mark planets with radioactive territories that have Desolate and Virulent traits.

warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.cost_or_limit: Their number depends on development; orbital habitats typically create 1d5 zones, colonies may create a second on an 8+ roll, and Voidfarer worlds have many minor zones plus 2d5 larger ones.
warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.go_wrong: Radiation supplies the harmful effect otherwise associated with toxins.
warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.combines: Can coexist with settlements, fortresses, and orbital habitats.
warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.mechanism: persistent environmental hazard and territory generation
warhammer-40k.rule.rak-gol-rad-zones.blocked_reason: The rules require persistent, trait-bearing zones whose number is generated by rolls.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-storms-isolate-w.name: Warp storms isolate worlds

effect.summary: Warp storms can sever worlds from their neighbours and foster long isolation.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-storms-isolate-w.go_wrong: Isolated worlds may decline into ruins or primitive societies.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-storms-isolate-w.combines: Can contribute to the decline of a former spacefaring realm.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-contamination-ca.name: Warp contamination can awaken when life arrives

effect.summary: The arrival of living explorers may stir dormant Warp powers into action.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-contamination-ca.cost_or_limit: The trigger is the arrival of life.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-contamination-ca.combines: May threaten visitors to devastated regions.

warhammer-40k.rule.local-phenomena-affec.name: Local Phenomena affect a world or site

effect.summary: Natural perils can change the challenges explorers face across a world or at a single site.

warhammer-40k.rule.local-phenomena-affec.cost_or_limit: The GM applies hazards to a whole world or one encounter site.
warhammer-40k.rule.local-phenomena-affec.blocked_reason: The effect may cover an entire world or site, which the basic grammar cannot model as a field.

warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.name: Mob Rule

effect.summary: Each nearby same-kind Ork or Gretchin raises the creature’s Willpower to resist Fear and Pinning.

warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.cost_or_limit: Each additional ally within 10 metres adds 10 Willpower.
warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.mind: Improves resistance to Fear and Pinning.
warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.who_may: Orks and Gretchin with this trait.
warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.combines: Strength depends on nearby members of the same kind.
warhammer-40k.rule.mob-rule.blocked_reason: The effect depends on counting nearby allies within a radius.

warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.name: Genestealer’s Kiss

effect.summary: A Genestealer implants genetic material into a host, beginning infection and psychic control.

warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.cost_or_limit: The infection develops over generations and may take centuries to spread.
warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.go_wrong: The host and descendants become devoted to the cult.
warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.mind: Infected hosts fall under the Patriarch’s psychic dominion.
warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.combines: Creates hybrid generations connected through the Broodmind.
warhammer-40k.rule.genestealer-s-kiss.blocked_reason: The mechanism changes inherited biology and also imposes psychic control.

warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.name: Broodlord’s Genestealer’s Kiss enthrallment

effect.summary: An infected victim becomes enthralled and obeys the Broodlord’s psychic commands.

warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.cost_or_limit: The victim must fail a Difficult Toughness test; enthrallment begins after 2d10+4 hours.
warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.go_wrong: The victim loses independent control and obeys commands.
warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.where_from: A bite that transmits alien genetic material.
warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.combines: Can be treated with a Very Hard Medicae test and a week of advanced care.
warhammer-40k.rule.broodlord-s-genesteal.blocked_reason: The infection produces prolonged obedience to another being’s psychic commands.

warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.name: Tomb null areas

effect.summary: Some tomb areas cut psykers and navigators off from the Warp.

warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.cost_or_limit: The effect lasts until they leave the null area.
warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.go_wrong: Affected psykers may suffer shock, agitation, and near-helplessness.
warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.mind: May cause extreme agitation and a Mental Trauma Test.
warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.who_may: Psykers and navigators entering the null area.
warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.combines: Also blocks psychic divination and can hinder vision with darkness.
warhammer-40k.rule.tomb-null-areas.blocked_reason: The effect suppresses access to the Warp throughout a location.

warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-repair-res.name: Archeotech repair restriction

effect.summary: Repairing damaged archeotech requires a successful Challenging Forbidden Lore (Archeotech) test before repair can begin.

warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-repair-res.cost_or_limit: The test is required before any repair attempt.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-repair-res.go_wrong: Failed access to the required knowledge prevents repair from starting.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-repair-res.where_from: Archeotech’s venerable design and lost manufacturing knowledge.
warhammer-40k.rule.archeotech-repair-res.blocked_reason: A prerequisite test can be represented as a condition on repair.

warhammer-40k.rule.imposing.name: Imposing

effect.summary: An imposing item bolsters intimidation and command; armor may also grant Air of Authority.

warhammer-40k.rule.imposing.cost_or_limit: Weapons grant +10 to Intimidate and Command; armor grants those bonuses and Air of Authority; gear grants +20 to visible-use opposed tests; ship components grant +10 to command and intimidation aboard ship.
warhammer-40k.rule.imposing.who_may: The item’s wielder, wearer, owner, or vessel commanders, depending on item type.
warhammer-40k.rule.imposing.combines: Effects vary by weapon, armor, gear, or ship component.
warhammer-40k.rule.imposing.blocked_reason: The quirk makes equipment carry ongoing bonuses and, in some cases, a talent.

warhammer-40k.rule.compact.name: Compact

effect.summary: The item is miniaturized, reducing its weight or space needs and making it harder to find when concealed.

warhammer-40k.rule.compact.cost_or_limit: Weapons and gear weigh half; armor weighs half; ship component Space falls by 4 to a minimum based on installation; concealment penalties vary by item type.
warhammer-40k.rule.compact.combines: Applies differently to weapons, armor, gear, and ship components.

warhammer-40k.rule.orks-can-alter-local-.go_wrong: Ork weapons may fall apart outside a WAAAGH!
warhammer-40k.rule.orks-can-alter-local-.mechanism: Collective belief alters local physical laws
warhammer-40k.rule.orks-can-alter-local-.blocked_reason: It changes how laws and technology work across an area through a collective field.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-disciplines-l.name: Psychic disciplines limit learning

effect.summary: Psykers normally learn from one discipline, while Aeldari or those with Warped Mind can learn beyond that limit; all may learn Minor Powers and Smite.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-disciplines-l.cost_or_limit: Aeldari have access to Divination, Runes of Battle, and one other discipline; others select one
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-disciplines-l.blocked_reason: This is an advancement limit, not a world effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.exchanging-psychic-po.name: Exchanging psychic powers adds risk

effect.summary: A Psyker may swap a known power for a randomly rolled power in the same discipline, with possible XP gain or loss.

warhammer-40k.rule.exchanging-psychic-po.cost_or_limit: At session start; exchange may change total XP
warhammer-40k.rule.exchanging-psychic-po.go_wrong: Adds a Wrath Die to Psychic Mastery tests for the session; a session-start Wrath Die roll of 1 adds Corruption
warhammer-40k.rule.exchanging-psychic-po.blocked_reason: The rule concerns changing a character’s available powers and is directly usable as a procedure.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-psychic-powe.name: Only one psychic power may be activated per Round

effect.summary: A Psyker can activate no more than one power during a Round.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-psychic-powe.blocked_reason: This is a direct limit on power use.

warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.name: A 1 on a Wrath Die triggers Perils of the Warp

effect.summary: Any 1 on a Wrath Die during a Psychic Mastery test causes a Perils result even if the power succeeds.

warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.cost_or_limit: Each additional 1 adds 10 to the d66 result
warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.go_wrong: Warp manifestation from the Perils table
warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.mind: May cause possession or other mental harm
warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.combines: Wrath Dice; Perils of the Warp
warhammer-40k.rule.a-1-on-a-wrath-die-tr.blocked_reason: The rule calls for varied adverse effects, some outside the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.power-level-restricti.name: Power level restrictions persist for the scene

effect.summary: After an Unbound test, subsequent tests must be Unbound or Transcendent; after a Transcendent test, they must be Transcendent.

warhammer-40k.rule.power-level-restricti.cost_or_limit: Lasts for the rest of the scene
warhammer-40k.rule.power-level-restricti.blocked_reason: This is a direct use restriction.

warhammer-40k.rule.perils-consequences-m.name: Perils consequences may automatically defeat ordinary NPCs

effect.summary: The Gamemaster may have Troop-threat characters and bystanders always fail specified tests caused by Perils.

warhammer-40k.rule.perils-consequences-m.go_wrong: Makes Psykers more dangerous to nearby people
warhammer-40k.rule.perils-consequences-m.mind: Can expose bystanders to fear and other consequences
warhammer-40k.rule.perils-consequences-m.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure rather than a world mechanism.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustaining-psychic-po.name: Sustaining psychic powers increases test difficulty

effect.summary: Each sustained power adds two to the difficulty of all the user's tests; each additional sustained power adds another two.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustaining-psychic-po.cost_or_limit: The penalty accumulates for each power maintained.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustaining-psychic-po.where_from: The strain of maintaining psychic effects.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustaining-psychic-po.combines: Applies alongside other test difficulty modifiers.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustaining-psychic-po.blocked_reason: A numerical difficulty modifier can be applied directly.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-can-break-sust.name: Damage can break sustained powers

effect.summary: After external damage, a sustaining psyker tests Willpower against damage suffered plus sustaining penalties; failure ends sustained powers.

warhammer-40k.rule.damage-can-break-sust.cost_or_limit: The test difficulty equals Wounds and Shock suffered plus the sustaining penalty.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-can-break-sust.who_may: Psykers sustaining powers who suffer external damage.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-can-break-sust.combines: Sustained powers may also cause their own Shock costs, which do not trigger this test.
warhammer-40k.rule.damage-can-break-sust.blocked_reason: A test can determine whether active effects end.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.name: Sustained powers may inflict periodic Shock

effect.summary: Some powers cause the psyker Shock at the end of each round or other interval specified by the power.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.cost_or_limit: The interval and amount are specified by the power; this self-inflicted Shock does not trigger the concentration test.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.go_wrong: The psyker accumulates Shock while maintaining the effect.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.who_may: Psykers using powers with this drawback.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.combines: Does not provoke the damage-interruption test.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers-may-.blocked_reason: Periodic Shock loss and its exception are straightforward costs.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-psychic-powe.name: Only one psychic power can be activated per round

effect.summary: A character can activate only one psychic power in a round; sustaining one does not count as activating it.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-psychic-powe.combines: Sustaining does not consume an activation.
warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-psychic-powe.blocked_reason: The restriction is a direct per-round limit.

warhammer-40k.rule.multi-target-powers-i.name: Multi-target powers increase activation difficulty

effect.summary: A multi-target power adds two to its activation difficulty for each target beyond the first, using one test for all targets.

warhammer-40k.rule.multi-target-powers-i.cost_or_limit: One test succeeds or fails against all chosen targets.
warhammer-40k.rule.multi-target-powers-i.go_wrong: A failed test fails against all targets.
warhammer-40k.rule.multi-target-powers-i.blocked_reason: The rule resolves one use of a power against multiple targets.

warhammer-40k.rule.a-psyker-must-maintai.name: A psyker must maintain concentration to sustain powers

effect.summary: A sustained power remains active while the psyker maintains it, and the psyker may stop at any time.

warhammer-40k.rule.a-psyker-must-maintai.cost_or_limit: Sustaining imposes test penalties and may cause power-specific strain.
warhammer-40k.rule.a-psyker-must-maintai.combines: Can maintain multiple powers with cumulative difficulty penalties.
warhammer-40k.rule.a-psyker-must-maintai.blocked_reason: The rule describes the duration and voluntary termination of ongoing effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.name: Warp exposure causes Corruption

effect.summary: Warp influence, sorcery, daemons, tainted items, and certain acts can corrupt people and reality.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.cost_or_limit: The GM calls for a Corruption Test when a character encounters an appropriate source; exposure in the Warp immediately causes Corruption, while shielded travel can corrupt over time.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.go_wrong: Failure can add Corruption Points; a failed test with a Complication doubles the gain.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.mind: Corruption can afflict the mind as well as deform the body.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.who_may: Characters exposed to sources of Corruption.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.where_from: The Warp and associated malign influences.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.combines: Psyker powers, daemons, tainted items, radiation, heresy, violence, and depravity can be sources.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.mechanism: Corruption tests and accumulating Corruption Points.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-exposure-causes-.blocked_reason: It describes accumulating corruption and mutation from many sources, beyond a single basic effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.name: Corruption Level progression

effect.summary: Corruption Points determine a character’s Corruption Level and raise the difficulty of future Corruption Tests.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.cost_or_limit: The listed levels progress from Pure through Chaos Spawn as Corruption Points rise.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.go_wrong: At Level 5 the character becomes an irredeemable Chaos Spawn, insane and controlled by the GM.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.mind: High Corruption can drive insanity and damnation.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.where_from: Warp influence and other corruption sources.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.combines: Higher levels modify Corruption Tests and can lead to mutation tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.mechanism: Threshold progression with transformation at the final threshold.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-level-prog.blocked_reason: It defines an irreversible character fate and transfer of control at the final level.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.name: Mutation Test and mutation accumulation

effect.summary: When Corruption Level increases, a failed Mutation Test grants a mutation whose severity and result are determined by tables.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.cost_or_limit: The test uses Conviction against a difficulty modified by Corruption Level; prior mutations add 10 to the later d66 result; duplicate mutations are rerolled unless they can differ.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.go_wrong: Mutations can deform flesh and mind and make social life harder.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.mind: Some mutations alter or damage the mind.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.combines: Mutation tables determine the form and effect; removing a mutated body part removes its associated benefit or detriment but not Corruption.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.mechanism: Threshold-triggered mutation test and random trait acquisition.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-test-and-mut.blocked_reason: It grants lasting changes to a character’s body and sometimes mind.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.name: Psychic powers expose users to Corruption

effect.summary: Using psychic powers opens the psyker and nearby people to Corruption, with greater or poorly controlled power increasing the danger.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.cost_or_limit: The possibility of a daemon using the psyker as a portal to the Materium is part of the risk.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.go_wrong: Psykers can corrupt themselves and companions or become portals for daemons.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.mind: Corruption can deform the body and afflict the mind.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.combines: The GM determines when a Corruption Test is required.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.mechanism: Risk of Corruption from power use.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-powers-expose.blocked_reason: The rule describes a variable, escalating harmful consequence attached to power use.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.name: Corruption Tests

effect.summary: A Conviction test against a source difficulty determines whether Corruption Points are gained.

warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.cost_or_limit: The character’s Corruption Level can increase the test difficulty; a single Wrath can reduce it by one, but not below 1.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.go_wrong: Failure grants Corruption Points equal to the shortfall and gives the GM Ruin; a failed Complication doubles the points; a Wrath Critical lowers difficulty by 2.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.mind: Corruption may sully the mind and soul.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.who_may: Characters encountering a Corruption source, with a chance to resist.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.where_from: The GM assigns a source difficulty.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.combines: Sources include Warp exposure, daemons, psychic powers, violence, depravity, radiation, and heresy.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.mechanism: Conviction test, point gain, and escalating difficulty.
warhammer-40k.rule.corruption-tests.blocked_reason: It requires test resolution, resource changes, and cumulative harmful progression.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.name: Mutation Tests

effect.summary: A failed Conviction test can grant a mutation when Corruption Level rises.

warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.cost_or_limit: Difficulty 3 is modified by Corruption Level; the player may choose to fail; previous mutations add 10 to the d66 result.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.go_wrong: A duplicate mutation requires a reroll unless a distinct effect is possible.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.mind: Mutations may twist the mind as well as the body.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.combines: Mutation severity and results come from the mutation tables; removing a mutated part removes related effects but does not reduce Corruption.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.mechanism: Corruption-triggered test and random mutation tables.
warhammer-40k.rule.mutation-tests.blocked_reason: The rule grants lasting randomized changes to body and mind.

warhammer-40k.rule.visible-aberration-so.name: Visible Aberration social penalty

effect.summary: Visible mutations impose a minimum +2 DN to social interactions with characters lacking the relevant Keyword.

warhammer-40k.rule.visible-aberration-so.cost_or_limit: Applies when the mutation is visible and the target lacks the specified Keyword.
warhammer-40k.rule.visible-aberration-so.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward rule modifying social-test difficulty.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-straits-of-andras.name: The Straits of Andrastre

effect.summary: A seemingly safe route through the Warp storm was an Empyrean mirage that destroyed or lost many vessels before a successful passage was found.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-straits-of-andras.cost_or_limit: Travel through the route is perilous and does not guarantee safe arrival.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-straits-of-andras.go_wrong: Ships can break apart or be lost forever on Warp shoals.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-straits-of-andras.where_from: The Warp storm of the Great Rift.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-straits-of-andras.blocked_reason: The rule describes a journey hazard and can be adjudicated without a missing effect capability.

warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.name: Throne Mechanicum echoes

effect.summary: A Knight pilot mentally controls the war machine through its Throne Mechanicum, while echoes of past pilots affect the current user.

warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.cost_or_limit: The device links the pilot’s senses and direction to the Knight.
warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.go_wrong: Past pilots’ mindsets influence the current pilot.
warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.mind: The user is affected by predecessor mindsets, reinforcing honour, protection of charges, and isolation.
warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.combines: Controls an Imperial Knight and links its senses and weapons to the pilot.
warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.mechanism: mind-machine link and inherited mental imprint
warhammer-40k.rule.throne-mechanicum-ech.blocked_reason: The rule includes an ongoing mental influence from prior pilots that the basic effect grammar cannot model.

warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation.name: Daemon manifestation

effect.summary: Daemons need a crossing point, summoning circle, or possessing mortal to manifest in reality.

warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation.cost_or_limit: Requires a route from the Warp into reality.
warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation.combines: Warp rifts, summoning, and possession are alternatives.
warhammer-40k.rule.daemon-manifestation.blocked_reason: The rule describes a summoning and manifestation requirement that basic effects do not model.

warhammer-40k.rule.ork-spore-survival.name: Ork spore survival

effect.summary: Ork spores can take root if any part of an Ork is left behind.

warhammer-40k.rule.ork-spore-survival.cost_or_limit: Every atom must be removed to prevent spore release and growth.
warhammer-40k.rule.ork-spore-survival.go_wrong: Surviving spores can lead to further Orks.
warhammer-40k.rule.ork-spore-survival.combines: Fire is recommended as a way to remove the threat.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-infinity-circuit.name: The Infinity Circuit

effect.summary: A Craftworld’s circuit houses the still-conscious souls of deceased Aeldari, whose psychic power helps power the vessel.

warhammer-40k.rule.the-infinity-circuit.cost_or_limit: The souls are not truly alive.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-infinity-circuit.who_may: Aeldari souls housed in a Craftworld’s circuit
warhammer-40k.rule.the-infinity-circuit.combines: Spirit Stones can place departed souls into wraithbone constructs.
warhammer-40k.rule.the-infinity-circuit.blocked_reason: The mechanism requires conscious deceased souls to persist and power structures.

warhammer-40k.rule.special-keywords.name: Special Keywords

effect.summary: A special keyword may be replaced by another suitable keyword.

warhammer-40k.rule.special-keywords.blocked_reason: The keyword choice is a straightforward character option.

warhammer-40k.rule.bracketed-keywords.name: Bracketed Keywords

effect.summary: A bracketed keyword is replaced by the selected specific sub-faction keyword.

warhammer-40k.rule.bracketed-keywords.blocked_reason: A keyword replacement is directly representable.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.name: Rogue Trader Dynasty inheritance

effect.summary: A Warrant of Trade and the associated wealth and influence may be inherited across generations.

warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.cost_or_limit: Dynasties differ in inherited resources and reputation.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.where_from: Warrant of Trade and family lineage
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.combines: Examples include Varonius, Kahlixian, and Armengarde.
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.mechanism: hereditary transfer of authority and resources
warhammer-40k.rule.rogue-trader-dynasty-.blocked_reason: The rule transfers a Warrant’s authority, wealth, and influence between generations.

warhammer-40k.rule.wargear-keywords.name: Wargear Keywords

effect.summary: Wargear keywords classify equipment and can matter to certain Talents.

warhammer-40k.rule.wargear-keywords.combines: Relevant to Talents such as Armourbane and Dual Wield.
warhammer-40k.rule.wargear-keywords.blocked_reason: Keyword tags can be handled as ordinary item properties.

warhammer-40k.rule.payment.name: Payment

effect.summary: Agents receive a payment grade and living expenses between missions.

warhammer-40k.rule.payment.cost_or_limit: Standard payment is 100 solars per agent every few days of active duty; other grades are 50, 200, and 600 solars.
warhammer-40k.rule.payment.go_wrong: Boons or liabilities can change the grade.
warhammer-40k.rule.payment.combines: Boons and liabilities can alter payment.
warhammer-40k.rule.payment.blocked_reason: Payment grades and timing can be represented as ordinary resource rules.

warhammer-40k.rule.boons-and-liabilities.name: Boons and Liabilities

effect.summary: A Patron starts with a free boon and a liability; additional boons may bring more liabilities.

warhammer-40k.rule.boons-and-liabilities.cost_or_limit: Each Patron starts with one of each; up to three additional boons may be selected, with the GM potentially adding a liability for each.
warhammer-40k.rule.boons-and-liabilities.go_wrong: Liabilities can harm the party or Patron.
warhammer-40k.rule.boons-and-liabilities.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward creation and selection rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.territorial.name: Territorial

effect.summary: The Patron pushes the group to secure land and establish bases, costing time.

warhammer-40k.rule.territorial.cost_or_limit: Can consume time during or between missions.
warhammer-40k.rule.territorial.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.territorial.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward time-cost rule.

warhammer-40k.rule.tithe-obsessed.name: Tithe Obsessed

effect.summary: The Patron docks pay for unjustified collateral damage.

warhammer-40k.rule.tithe-obsessed.cost_or_limit: Applies to collateral damage the group cannot justify.
warhammer-40k.rule.tithe-obsessed.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.tithe-obsessed.blocked_reason: The penalty is a direct loss of pay.

warhammer-40k.rule.unorthodox-beliefs.name: Unorthodox Beliefs

effect.summary: Joining the Patron’s rituals can reduce the group’s between-mission time.

warhammer-40k.rule.unorthodox-beliefs.cost_or_limit: The Patron has −2 Influence with the Adeptus Ministorum.
warhammer-40k.rule.unorthodox-beliefs.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.unorthodox-beliefs.blocked_reason: The stated effects are time and Influence changes.

warhammer-40k.rule.saboteur.name: Saboteur

effect.summary: The Patron orders non-lethal sabotage against two loathed Factions when encountered.

warhammer-40k.rule.saboteur.cost_or_limit: The Patron has −1 Influence with each targeted Faction.
warhammer-40k.rule.saboteur.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.saboteur.blocked_reason: The stated effects are direct mission and Influence changes.

warhammer-40k.rule.shaky-authority.name: Shaky Authority

effect.summary: On a d10 result of 0, the Patron’s positive Influence is ignored.

warhammer-40k.rule.shaky-authority.cost_or_limit: Roll a d10 whenever using Patron Influence.
warhammer-40k.rule.shaky-authority.go_wrong: A roll of 0 nullifies the positive Influence.
warhammer-40k.rule.shaky-authority.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.shaky-authority.blocked_reason: A direct conditional rule can implement the stated effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy-supplies.name: Shoddy Supplies

effect.summary: The Patron’s supplied gear has the Shoddy Flaw.

warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy-supplies.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy-supplies.blocked_reason: The passage does not define the Shoddy Flaw’s effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.name: Sidereal Quests

effect.summary: The Patron assigns favors owed on visited worlds, diverting time from the main mission.

warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.cost_or_limit: Refusing may create an enemy and anger the Patron.
warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.go_wrong: The group may lose time or make enemies.
warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.where_from: Favors owed across worlds and cities.
warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.combines: Tasks can include guarding, negotiations, or courier work.
warhammer-40k.rule.sidereal-quests.blocked_reason: This is a direct mission complication.

warhammer-40k.rule.strange-tastes.name: Strange Tastes

effect.summary: The Patron secretly demands a rare, possibly illegal object or substance.

warhammer-40k.rule.strange-tastes.cost_or_limit: The desired thing is determined by the Gamemaster.
warhammer-40k.rule.strange-tastes.go_wrong: The request may violate Imperial law.
warhammer-40k.rule.strange-tastes.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.strange-tastes.blocked_reason: The demand itself is playable without additional effect mechanics.

warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.name: Suspect

effect.summary: Suspicious Factions may tail or surveil the group if it reveals its Patron.

warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.cost_or_limit: The Patron has −2 Influence with a suspicious Faction, often the Inquisition.
warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.go_wrong: Enemies may interfere while seeking evidence.
warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.who_may: A Patron may have this liability.
warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.where_from: Faction suspicions linking the Patron to crime or heresy.
warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.combines: The group’s revealed affiliation can trigger surveillance.
warhammer-40k.rule.suspect.blocked_reason: Surveillance and Influence changes are straightforward game effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.influence.name: Influence

effect.summary: Each applicable Influence point adds one SL to social Tests with the relevant Faction or subject.

warhammer-40k.rule.influence.cost_or_limit: Influence is tracked by Faction and may also vary for individuals or groups.
warhammer-40k.rule.influence.go_wrong: Negative Influence is kept secret from players; use of a Patron’s positive Influence can fail under Shaky Authority.
warhammer-40k.rule.influence.where_from: Faction relationships, connections, knowledge, or leverage.
warhammer-40k.rule.influence.combines: Faction and individual Influence can stack cumulatively.
warhammer-40k.rule.influence.blocked_reason: A numeric modifier to social Tests is directly implementable.

warhammer-40k.rule.adeptus-astra-telepat.name: Adeptus Astra Telepathica duty equipment

effect.summary: A character choosing one of the listed duties receives a knife, robes, a divination instrument, and 100 solars.

warhammer-40k.rule.adeptus-astra-telepat.cost_or_limit: Applies to the described duty choices.
warhammer-40k.rule.adeptus-astra-telepat.blocked_reason: A fixed equipment grant is directly implementable.

warhammer-40k.rule.soul-binding-ritual.name: soul-binding ritual

effect.summary: A ritual gives some psykers a portion of the Emperor’s power.

warhammer-40k.rule.soul-binding-ritual.mind: It fortifies minds against Warp terrors.
warhammer-40k.rule.soul-binding-ritual.combines: The Emperor’s power and mental fortification.
warhammer-40k.rule.soul-binding-ritual.blocked_reason: The rite’s transfer of the Emperor’s power and its mental protection require mechanics beyond the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.vow-of-tranquillity.name: Vow of Tranquillity

effect.summary: A vow that Sister-in-Waiting characters have not yet taken and that is associated with their silence.

warhammer-40k.rule.vow-of-tranquillity.cost_or_limit: A Sister-in-Waiting may still speak before taking it.
warhammer-40k.rule.vow-of-tranquillity.blocked_reason: The vow’s actual restrictions are not specified.

warhammer-40k.rule.maximum-skill-advance.name: Maximum Skill Advances during Character Creation

effect.summary: A character can take no more than two advances in a single skill and one in a specialisation during creation.

warhammer-40k.rule.maximum-skill-advance.cost_or_limit: Two per skill; one per specialisation.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel-time-dila.name: Warp travel time dilation

effect.summary: A traveler may experience days or weeks while months or years pass before arrival.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel-time-dila.cost_or_limit: The time difference complicates interstellar travel.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel-time-dila.who_may: Warp travelers are subject to it.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel-time-dila.mechanism: Variable elapsed time during warp journeys.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-travel-time-dila.blocked_reason: The rule describes time dilation, a temporal effect not supported by the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds-death.name: Critical Wounds death threshold

effect.summary: A character dies at the start of their next turn if their Critical Wounds exceed their Toughness Bonus at the end of their turn.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds-death.cost_or_limit: The maximum Critical Wounds equals Toughness Bonus.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds-death.mechanism: Delayed death from exceeding a wound threshold.

warhammer-40k.rule.fate.name: FATE

effect.summary: Fate can be spent for benefits or permanently burned to escape dire circumstances.

warhammer-40k.rule.fate.cost_or_limit: Characters begin with three Fate; spent Fate returns each session, but burned Fate returns only through exceptional service or sacrifice.
warhammer-40k.rule.fate.go_wrong: Burning Fate permanently reduces the resource unless a qualifying deed restores it.
warhammer-40k.rule.fate.where_from: Determination, destiny, or the Emperor’s favour.
warhammer-40k.rule.fate.combines: Spending and burning Fate offer different benefits.
warhammer-40k.rule.fate.blocked_reason: The resource changes and its recovery conditions can be represented directly.

warhammer-40k.rule.off-hand-disadvantage.name: Off-hand Disadvantage

effect.summary: A test using only the character’s off hand is made with Disadvantage.

warhammer-40k.rule.off-hand-disadvantage.cost_or_limit: Applies when only the off hand is used.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touch-requiremen.name: Warp touch requirement

effect.summary: Psychic Mastery may require a character to have been touched by the Warp.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touch-requiremen.cost_or_limit: The listed requirement must be met unless the GM waives it.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touch-requiremen.where_from: Character history or a Talent, depending on the skill.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touch-requiremen.combines: Psychic Mastery is named as an example.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touch-requiremen.mechanism: Prerequisite gate for learning a restricted skill.

warhammer-40k.rule.availability-categori.name: Availability categories

effect.summary: Equipment is Common, Scarce, Rare, or Exotic; scarcity governs whether it can be found.

warhammer-40k.rule.availability-categori.cost_or_limit: Scarce and Rare require a successful local test; Exotic requires GM approval, commissioning, or crafting.
warhammer-40k.rule.availability-categori.go_wrong: Failed tests mean the item is unavailable locally.

warhammer-40k.rule.availability-test.name: Availability Test

effect.summary: Roll 1d100 against the listed chance; equal or lower means the item is in stock.

warhammer-40k.rule.availability-test.cost_or_limit: A failed test can be retried on a new planet or a week later if trade routes are open.
warhammer-40k.rule.availability-test.go_wrong: Failure means no stock at that time and place.

warhammer-40k.rule.stock-quantities.name: Stock quantities

effect.summary: Stock depends on world type; Common stock is generally doubled and Rare stock halved, rounded up.

warhammer-40k.rule.stock-quantities.cost_or_limit: Feral and Feudal worlds generally have one item; Shrine and Reclaimed worlds 1d10; Hive and Forge quantities are GM-set.
warhammer-40k.rule.stock-quantities.combines: Applies after an item is found in stock.

warhammer-40k.rule.haggling-prices.name: Haggling prices

effect.summary: A successful Rapport (Haggle) test reduces a purchase price by 5% per SL, up to 20%.

warhammer-40k.rule.haggling-prices.cost_or_limit: A failed opposed test may leave the price unchanged, raise it by up to 10%, or end the sale.
warhammer-40k.rule.haggling-prices.go_wrong: An offended seller may refuse to sell.
warhammer-40k.rule.haggling-prices.combines: Logic (Evaluation) can assess qualities and value.

warhammer-40k.rule.second-hand-sale-pric.name: Second-hand sale price

effect.summary: An item's base selling price is half its listed cost, rounded up.

warhammer-40k.rule.second-hand-sale-pric.cost_or_limit: A buyer must be available locally; bargaining can further affect the deal.
warhammer-40k.rule.second-hand-sale-pric.go_wrong: A buyer may not be found.
warhammer-40k.rule.second-hand-sale-pric.combines: Registered Trader modifies this base price.

warhammer-40k.rule.lowering-the-price.name: Lowering the price

effect.summary: Each time a seller halves their asking price, the buyer's Availability improves by one step.

warhammer-40k.rule.lowering-the-price.cost_or_limit: Price reductions are cumulative and lower the proceeds.
warhammer-40k.rule.lowering-the-price.who_may: A seller unable to find a buyer.

warhammer-40k.rule.barter-ratio.name: Barter ratio

effect.summary: Trade quantities are based on approximate value units and the Availability of the goods exchanged.

warhammer-40k.rule.barter-ratio.cost_or_limit: Compare listed prices to form equal-value packages, then apply the Availability ratio.
warhammer-40k.rule.barter-ratio.go_wrong: Unequal package values require different quantities to balance the deal.
warhammer-40k.rule.barter-ratio.combines: Availability determines how many units change hands.

warhammer-40k.rule.item-quality-and-flaw.name: Item Quality and Flaw pricing

effect.summary: Each Item Quality doubles listed price and improves Availability by one step; qualities and flaws indicate relative craftsmanship.

warhammer-40k.rule.item-quality-and-flaw.cost_or_limit: Availability cannot be improved beyond its category limits as determined by the wider rules.
warhammer-40k.rule.item-quality-and-flaw.combines: Qualities improve function; Flaws worsen it and make the item easier to find.
warhammer-40k.rule.item-quality-and-flaw.blocked_reason: The rule changes an item's persistent quality and availability state.

warhammer-40k.rule.item-flaws.name: Item Flaws

effect.summary: Flaws reduce price and improve availability; excess flaws may make equipment poor quality.

warhammer-40k.rule.item-flaws.cost_or_limit: Each flaw halves listed price, rounded up, and improves Availability by one step; Exotic availability is unchanged.
warhammer-40k.rule.item-flaws.combines: More flaws than Qualities may invite derision.
warhammer-40k.rule.item-flaws.blocked_reason: This is an equipment rule, not an unsupported effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.encumbrance-capacity.name: Encumbrance capacity

effect.summary: Carrying beyond capacity causes movement and Agility penalties.

warhammer-40k.rule.encumbrance-capacity.cost_or_limit: Unpenalised capacity equals Strength Bonus plus Toughness Bonus; twice that amount causes Restrained.
warhammer-40k.rule.encumbrance-capacity.combines: Worn items reduce Encumbrance by one; oversized items are normally limited to one.
warhammer-40k.rule.encumbrance-capacity.blocked_reason: The rule maps to carrying capacity and conditions.

warhammer-40k.rule.master-crafted.name: Master Crafted

effect.summary: Improves relevant Tests or armour protection.

warhammer-40k.rule.master-crafted.cost_or_limit: Weapons, gear, and tools grant +1 SL to relevant Tests; armour gains +2 Armour.
warhammer-40k.rule.master-crafted.blocked_reason: The bonus can be represented as an equipment modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.ornamental.name: Ornamental

effect.summary: Impressive appearance can aid Fellowship Tests.

warhammer-40k.rule.ornamental.cost_or_limit: May be taken repeatedly; the GM may award +1 SL when the audience values the appearance.
warhammer-40k.rule.ornamental.blocked_reason: The effect is a conditional Test modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.durable.name: Durable

effect.summary: Prevents the first loss of armour or equipment function.

warhammer-40k.rule.durable.cost_or_limit: For a weapon, grants Reliable instead; otherwise prevents the first such failure.
warhammer-40k.rule.durable.blocked_reason: The first-failure protection can be tracked as a rule state.

warhammer-40k.rule.bulky.name: Bulky

effect.summary: Increases Encumbrance and removes Subtle.

warhammer-40k.rule.bulky.blocked_reason: The effect is an equipment modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy.name: Shoddy

effect.summary: Reduces Tests or armour protection.

warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy.cost_or_limit: Weapons, gear, and tools impose −10% on relevant Tests; armour loses 2 Armour, to a minimum of 1.
warhammer-40k.rule.shoddy.blocked_reason: The effect is an equipment modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.ugly.name: Ugly

effect.summary: Unsightly equipment can hinder Fellowship Tests.

warhammer-40k.rule.ugly.cost_or_limit: The GM may impose −1 SL when the audience cares about aesthetics.
warhammer-40k.rule.ugly.blocked_reason: The effect is a conditional Test modifier.

warhammer-40k.rule.unreliable.name: Unreliable

effect.summary: Grants Unstable; an already Unstable item self-destructs when it jams.

warhammer-40k.rule.unreliable.go_wrong: An already Unstable item automatically self-destructs when it jams.
warhammer-40k.rule.unreliable.blocked_reason: The trigger and failure can be represented with item state.

warhammer-40k.rule.chain-power-and-shock.name: Chain, Power, and Shock weapon activation

effect.summary: Activating the micro-reactor enables a weapon’s special Traits.

warhammer-40k.rule.chain-power-and-shock.cost_or_limit: Activation is a Free Action and is usually needed for the unique Traits.
warhammer-40k.rule.chain-power-and-shock.where_from: Micro-reactor in the handle or an external pack
warhammer-40k.rule.chain-power-and-shock.combines: Applies to Chain, Power, and Shock weapons.
warhammer-40k.rule.chain-power-and-shock.blocked_reason: The weapon’s Traits depend on whether its power source is active.

warhammer-40k.rule.force-weapon-psyker-b.name: Force weapon psyker bonus

effect.summary: A Psyker user adds current Warp Charge to damage, doubled against Daemons.

warhammer-40k.rule.force-weapon-psyker-b.cost_or_limit: Requires the Psyker Talent; the bonus equals current Warp Charge.
warhammer-40k.rule.force-weapon-psyker-b.who_may: A character with the Psyker Talent
warhammer-40k.rule.force-weapon-psyker-b.blocked_reason: This requires checking a character’s Talent and current Warp Charge.

warhammer-40k.rule.ammunition-availabili.name: Ammunition availability and price

effect.summary: Sets standard ammunition availability and magazine price relative to the weapon.

warhammer-40k.rule.ammunition-availabili.cost_or_limit: Standard ammunition is one Availability step lower, to Common minimum; a full magazine costs 10% of the weapon’s price.
warhammer-40k.rule.ammunition-availabili.combines: Custom ammunition can change weapon function.
warhammer-40k.rule.ammunition-availabili.blocked_reason: The rule is a price and availability calculation.

warhammer-40k.rule.explosives-are-single.name: Explosives are single-use

effect.summary: Explosives are consumed when used.

warhammer-40k.rule.explosives-are-single.cost_or_limit: All listed explosives are single-use and have Unstable.
warhammer-40k.rule.explosives-are-single.combines: Thrown, Ordnance, or Engineering specialisation determines use.
warhammer-40k.rule.explosives-are-single.blocked_reason: Consumption and item traits can be tracked directly.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-attachment-lim.name: Weapon attachment limits

effect.summary: Limits attachment combinations on a weapon.

warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-attachment-lim.cost_or_limit: A weapon may have one sight and one combat attachment, with no duplicate support attachments.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-attachment-lim.combines: Modifications generally require an hour and a successful Challenging Tech (Engineering) Test.
warhammer-40k.rule.weapon-attachment-lim.blocked_reason: The attachment limits can be tracked as item slots.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-force-field-.name: Only one force field active

effect.summary: A person can have only one force field active at once.

warhammer-40k.rule.only-one-force-field-.blocked_reason: Tracking multiple wearable field states requires an item-state capability.

warhammer-40k.rule.force-field-overload.name: Force field overload

effect.summary: Damage at least equal to a field’s Overload value collapses it until repaired.

warhammer-40k.rule.force-field-overload.cost_or_limit: Repair usually takes a Very Hard Tech Test and at least eight hours.
warhammer-40k.rule.force-field-overload.blocked_reason: A field’s working or collapsed state and repair recovery need item-state tracking.

warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-maximum.name: Augmetic maximum

effect.summary: A character cannot have more augmetics than their Toughness Bonus.

warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-maximum.cost_or_limit: Flesh is Weak can increase the maximum.
warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-maximum.blocked_reason: A numerical augmentation limit is a direct game constraint.

warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-repair.name: Augmetic repair

effect.summary: Augmetic limb critical wounds use Tech rather than Medicae, and a required kit is a Combi-Tool.

warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-repair.cost_or_limit: Broken bones require five extended-test successes and replacement parts worth 25% or 50% of the augmetic cost; amputation makes it irreparable.
warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-repair.go_wrong: A broken bone does not heal naturally; amputation requires replacement.
warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-repair.combines: Uses a Combi-Tool where a Chirurgeon’s Kit would ordinarily be required.
warhammer-40k.rule.augmetic-repair.blocked_reason: Repairing a damaged augmentation requires tracking its working condition and restoration.

warhammer-40k.rule.strength-in-steel-acc.name: Strength in Steel access

effect.summary: Advanced Strength in Steel augmetics are normally limited to Tech-Priests and their Adeptus Mechanicus servants.

warhammer-40k.rule.strength-in-steel-acc.cost_or_limit: The GM may allow access to others after notable service to Mars’s priesthood.
warhammer-40k.rule.strength-in-steel-acc.who_may: Tech-Priests or their servants, subject to the stated exception.
warhammer-40k.rule.strength-in-steel-acc.combines: Applies to the listed advanced augmetics.
warhammer-40k.rule.strength-in-steel-acc.blocked_reason: This is a direct access limit.

warhammer-40k.rule.poor-meal-fatigue.name: Poor-meal fatigue

effect.summary: A week of only Poor meals may leave a character Fatigued.

warhammer-40k.rule.poor-meal-fatigue.cost_or_limit: Requires a Challenging Fortitude (Endurance) Test; Fatigue lasts until a better meal is eaten.
warhammer-40k.rule.poor-meal-fatigue.who_may: Characters eating only Poor meals for a week

warhammer-40k.rule.golden-throne-sustena.name: Golden Throne sustenance

effect.summary: A thousand psykers are sacrificed each day to sustain the Emperor on the Golden Throne.

warhammer-40k.rule.golden-throne-sustena.go_wrong: Failure of this supply is not described.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-manifestation.name: Psychic manifestation

effect.summary: Using a power requires opening the mind to the Warp and succeeding at a Psychic Mastery test.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-manifestation.cost_or_limit: Manifestation is an Action unless a power says otherwise; difficulty is power-specific.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-manifestation.go_wrong: A failure leaves drawn psychic energy leaking into the psyker.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-manifestation.mind: Channeling risks sanity and causes physical stress signs.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-manifestation.combines: Successful tests apply the power; failure usually does not.

warhammer-40k.rule.target-awareness.name: Target awareness

effect.summary: A target must be known and located, normally by line of sight or a psychic sense.

warhammer-40k.rule.target-awareness.blocked_reason: Psychic target detection may require extrasensory perception.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-charge.name: Warp Charge

effect.summary: Manifesting powers accumulates Warp energy within the psyker.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-charge.cost_or_limit: Successful use adds the power’s Warp Rating; failure adds one per negative SL, up to that rating.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-charge.go_wrong: Exceeding the psyker’s threshold risks Perils of the Warp.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-charge.combines: Talents and circumstances can change the amount.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-manifest.name: Critical Manifest

effect.summary: A critical Manifest test reduces the power’s Warp Rating by the psyker’s Willpower Bonus, to a minimum of one.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-manifest.combines: Applies to a critical Manifest test.

warhammer-40k.rule.manifest-fumble.name: Manifest Fumble

effect.summary: A fumble doubles the Warp Charge normally gained.

warhammer-40k.rule.manifest-fumble.go_wrong: Increased Warp Charge raises the chance of peril.
warhammer-40k.rule.manifest-fumble.combines: Applies to a fumbled Manifest test.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers.name: Sustained powers

effect.summary: Concentration can extend certain powers indefinitely while the psyker remains conscious and pays their Warp Charge upkeep.

warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers.cost_or_limit: Warp Charge cannot fall below the combined Warp Ratings of sustained powers.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers.go_wrong: Perils immediately ends all sustained powers.
warhammer-40k.rule.sustained-powers.combines: Purgation cannot reduce charge below upkeep.

warhammer-40k.rule.pushing.name: Pushing

effect.summary: A psyker may gain Advantage on a Manifest test by taking additional Warp energy.

warhammer-40k.rule.pushing.cost_or_limit: Adds 1d10 Warp Charge regardless of success or failure.
warhammer-40k.rule.pushing.go_wrong: A failed fumble immediately triggers Perils of the Warp.

warhammer-40k.rule.overt-powers.name: Overt Powers

effect.summary: Overt powers make their effects and the psyker responsible obvious to witnesses.

warhammer-40k.rule.overt-powers.combines: Powers not marked Overt may be difficult to identify.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-threshold.name: Warp Threshold

effect.summary: A psyker’s safe Warp Charge limit equals their Willpower Bonus, subject to adjustments.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-threshold.cost_or_limit: Charge above the threshold risks Perils of the Warp.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-threshold.go_wrong: A failed containment test can cause a Warp manifestation.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-threshold.combines: Sanctioned Psyker Talent and other effects may adjust it.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-phenomena-dur.name: Psychic Phenomena duration

effect.summary: Phenomena normally affect the current Zone for 1d10 minutes or until the encounter ends.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-phenomena-dur.cost_or_limit: A repeated phenomenon in an already affected Zone creates a lasting anomaly.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-phenomena-dur.combines: Each result may specify different lingering consequences.
warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-phenomena-dur.blocked_reason: Persistent zone-wide phenomena need area and lingering-field effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-breakthrough.name: Psychic Breakthrough

effect.summary: A table result triggers another roll and applies both that result’s ordinary and lingering effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.psychic-breakthrough.go_wrong: The additional result may produce lasting effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.influence-is-not-mind.name: Influence is not mind control

effect.summary: Reputation with a faction does not override an individual’s motivations or compel compliance.

warhammer-40k.rule.influence-is-not-mind.cost_or_limit: Requests risking personal loss, shame, harm, or death may still be refused.
warhammer-40k.rule.influence-is-not-mind.who_may: Applies to interactions with faction members.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.name: Warp-touched Zone

effect.summary: A warp-tainted area boosts psychic tests, adds Warp Charge to powers, and can expose occupants to corruption.

warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.cost_or_limit: Psychic powers add Warp Charge equal to their SL; ending a turn there can require a Fortitude Test to avoid Corruption.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.go_wrong: Exposure can cause Corruption; the GM may also apply a Psychic Phenomena result.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.who_may: Affects psykers and anyone ending a turn in the zone.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.where_from: Warp-tainted environments where the veil is thin.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.combines: Interacts with psychic powers and the Psychic Phenomena Table.
warhammer-40k.rule.warp-touched-zone.blocked_reason: It changes conditions for an entire zone and exposes characters over time, which the basic effect grammar cannot fully model.

warhammer-40k.rule.melee-attack-procedur.name: Melee attack procedure

effect.summary: Melee attacks use a target, opposed test, hit location, armour reduction, and wounds.

warhammer-40k.rule.melee-attack-procedur.cost_or_limit: Target must be within Immediate Range.
warhammer-40k.rule.melee-attack-procedur.go_wrong: A critical or fumble can alter the outcome.
warhammer-40k.rule.melee-attack-procedur.combines: Weapon Damage, success levels, hit location, armour, and wounds.
warhammer-40k.rule.melee-attack-procedur.blocked_reason: The procedure can be run with attack, position, and damage effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.ranged-attack-procedu.name: Ranged attack procedure

effect.summary: Ranged attacks test against a target, then apply damage, hit location, armour, and ammunition use.

warhammer-40k.rule.ranged-attack-procedu.cost_or_limit: Target must be visible and within weapon range.
warhammer-40k.rule.ranged-attack-procedu.go_wrong: A missed test deals no damage; an out-of-range attack has Disadvantage.
warhammer-40k.rule.ranged-attack-procedu.combines: Dodge, weapon damage, success levels, hit location, armour, and ammunition.
warhammer-40k.rule.ranged-attack-procedu.blocked_reason: The procedure can be run with attack, position, and damage effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.fumbles.name: FUMBLES

effect.summary: Doubles on a negative-success attack roll trigger an unfortunate result from a fumble table.

warhammer-40k.rule.fumbles.cost_or_limit: Requires doubles and negative success levels.
warhammer-40k.rule.fumbles.go_wrong: The result may injure the attacker or cause another mishap.
warhammer-40k.rule.fumbles.combines: Can occur even if the attacker wins an opposed test.
warhammer-40k.rule.fumbles.blocked_reason: A conditional table result can be resolved as an alteration to the attack outcome.

warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.name: CRITICALS AND FUMBLES

effect.summary: Doubles on an attack roll with positive success levels cause a critical, while doubles with negative success levels cause a fumble.

warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.cost_or_limit: Depends on doubles and the sign of the success level.
warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.go_wrong: Fumbles may cause danger or self-injury.
warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.who_may: Attackers in melee or ranged combat.
warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.combines: Can apply even when an opposed test is lost or won.
warhammer-40k.rule.criticals-and-fumbles.blocked_reason: The trigger is clear, though the associated critical wound or mishap tables require additional resolution.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.name: Critical Wounds

effect.summary: Critical hits and damage beyond maximum Wounds inflict severe injuries with listed effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.cost_or_limit: Untreated Critical Wounds beyond Toughness Bonus cause the character to be Dying.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.go_wrong: Untreated injuries can lead to death.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.who_may: Characters receiving a critical hit or exceeding maximum Wounds.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.combines: Severity and hit location determine the injury.
warhammer-40k.rule.critical-wounds.blocked_reason: The injury table and death threshold require additional rule resolution beyond a basic effect.

warhammer-40k.rule.drowning-and-suffocat.name: Drowning and suffocation

effect.summary: After breath runs out, suffocation or drowning causes Wounds each round and eventual unconsciousness and death.

warhammer-40k.rule.drowning-and-suffocat.cost_or_limit: Prepared characters can hold breath for Toughness Bonus times ten seconds.
warhammer-40k.rule.drowning-and-suffocat.go_wrong: Damage ignores armour; unconscious characters die after rounds equal to Toughness Bonus.
warhammer-40k.rule.drowning-and-suffocat.combines: Maximum Wounds and Toughness Bonus determine the progression.
warhammer-40k.rule.drowning-and-suffocat.blocked_reason: The recurring damage and delayed death can be represented with vitality loss and a timer.

warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.name: Exposure

effect.summary: In hostile environments, repeated failed Fortitude tests impose penalties and may cause armour-ignoring damage.

warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.cost_or_limit: Tests are generally required every four hours, more often in extreme conditions.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.go_wrong: Continued failures can cause unconsciousness, Critical Wounds, and death.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.mind: Heat exposure can impair mental tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.where_from: Cold, heat, deserts, storms, and similar environments.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.combines: Some equipment improves or removes cold exposure tests; removing heavy clothing or armour helps against heat.
warhammer-40k.rule.exposure.blocked_reason: Periodic tests, penalties, and damage can be represented with the basic effect grammar.

warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.name: Thirst and starvation

effect.summary: Lack of food or water requires increasingly difficult tests and eventually causes penalties and damage.

warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.cost_or_limit: Water tests occur daily; food tests every three days; test difficulty worsens over time.
warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.go_wrong: Failures cause penalties and armour-ignoring damage; deprivation prevents healing and recovery from Fatigued.
warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.mind: Some effects impair Intelligence, Willpower, or Fellowship tests.
warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.who_may: Characters without sufficient food or water.
warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.combines: Fortitude (Endurance) tests and the Fatigued condition.
warhammer-40k.rule.thirst-and-starvation.blocked_reason: A timer, repeated tests, and damage can represent the described survival effects.

warhammer-40k.rule.healing-wounds.name: HEALING WOUNDS

effect.summary: Rest and successful medical care restore Wounds.

warhammer-40k.rule.healing-wounds.cost_or_limit: Natural healing is limited to once daily; medical healing is also limited daily, with another opportunity after a Critical Wound.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing-wounds.go_wrong: A failed medical test restores no Wounds but has no further ill effect.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing-wounds.who_may: Characters who rest or receive care from a trained ally.
warhammer-40k.rule.healing-wounds.combines: Healing amount depends on Toughness Bonus, success levels, or the healer’s Intelligence Bonus.
